1350.description: The Weighted Back Extension with Opposite Arm and Leg Reach is a compound exercise that targets the spinal erectors, glutes, and hamstrings, while also engaging the core muscles for stability.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor, with your legs extended and arms extended in front of you, holding a dumbbell or weight plate.
Engage your core and lift your torso, arms, and legs off the floor, reaching your opposite arm and leg out simultaneously.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, alternating between left and right for the desired number of repetitions.

1940.description: The Weighted Back Squat is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It is a fundamental strength-building exercise that improves overall lower body power and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across the back of your shoulders. Engage your core and maintain good posture throughout the movement.
Initiate the squat by sending your hips back as if you are sitting into a chair, keeping your chest up and your back flat.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as your mobility allows. Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward.
Press through your heels to drive back up to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

1941.description: The Weighted Balancing Squat is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups to improve overall strength, stability, and balance. This exercise challenges the body's core and lower body musculature while also requiring precise control and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Maintain an upright torso and engage your core as you slowly lower into a squat, keeping your weight evenly distributed through your heels.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the squat, then press through your heels to return to the starting position, maintaining control of the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on balance and proper form throughout the movement.

1110.description: The Weighted Barbell Rollout is a challenging core and upper body strength exercise that works the abdominal muscles, chest, and shoulders. It involves rolling a barbell out in front of you and then back to the starting position, building stability and anti-extension strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a shoulder-width grip at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels as you slowly roll the barbell out, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Pause briefly at the furthest point of the movement, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring you maintain control and tension throughout the movement.

1351.description: Weighted Base Rotations are a compound exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and hips, to improve rotational strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a weight plate or dumbbell at chest height with both hands.
Engage your core and slowly rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips stationary and the weight centered in front of your chest.
Pause briefly at the end of the range of motion, then rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the left side, maintaining control and stability throughout the movement.
Continue alternating between right and left rotations, keeping your core engaged and your movements smooth and controlled.

1563.description: The Weighted Bear Crawl is a full-body strength exercise that challenges stability, coordination, and muscular endurance. By adding weight, it increases the demand on the core, shoulders, and lower body to maintain proper form during the crawling motion.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell or weight plate at chest height.
Hinge at the hips to lower into a bear crawl position, keeping your back flat and core braced.
Maintain a neutral spine and engage your glutes as you crawl forward, alternating moving your right hand and left foot, then left hand and right foot.
Continue crawling for the desired distance or time, keeping your elbows close to your sides and applying even pressure through your hands and feet.

1942.description: The Weighted Bench Squat with Rotational Chop is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and core. It combines the benefits of a squat with a rotational movement, improving overall strength, stability, and power.
instructions: Stand behind a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Initiate the movement by sitting your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a squat, keeping your chest up and core engaged.
As you reach the bottom of the squat, rotate your torso to the left, bringing the weight across your body in a chopping motion.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, then repeat the squat and rotation to the right side.
Maintain control throughout the movement, focusing on stability and proper form.

1352.description: The Weighted Bent Knee Reverse Hyperextension is a strength-building exercise that targets the posterior chain muscles, including the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back. It helps improve core stability and functional strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell behind your head.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso until it's nearly parallel to the ground.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes as you slowly raise your torso back to the starting position, focusing on driving through your heels.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1274.description: The Weighted Bent Knee Swiss Ball Reverse Hip Raise targets the posterior chain, improving hip mobility, core stability, and lower body strength. It challenges the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back muscles.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your feet hip-width apart and knees bent at 90 degrees. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Slowly lower your hips toward the floor, keeping your knees bent, until your thighs are nearly parallel to the ground.
Squeeze your glutes and drive through your heels to raise your hips back up to the starting position, keeping your core braced.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment before repeating. Maintain control throughout the movement.

1878.description: The Weighted Bent Knee V Up is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It helps improve overall core stability and coordination.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms extended overhead.
Engage your core and simultaneously raise your arms, shoulders, and legs off the floor, creating a 'V' shape with your body.
Hold the V position briefly, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Throughout the movement, keep your knees bent and your arms extended overhead.

1165.description: The Weighted Bicycle Crunch is a compound abdominal exercise that engages multiple core muscles simultaneously, helping to strengthen the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands behind your head, elbows out to the sides.
Bend your knees and lift your feet off the floor, keeping your shins parallel to the ground.
Slowly bring your right elbow towards your left knee as you straighten your right leg, then repeat on the opposite side, alternating sides in a bicycle-like motion.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement and avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.

1049.description: The Weighted Bob and Weave Circle is a dynamic cardio exercise that engages various muscle groups while improving agility, coordination, and overall fitness. This exercise challenges the body to move through a circular pattern while maintaining control and balance.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a lightweight object (such as a medicine ball or dumbbell) at chest height.
Initiate the movement by stepping out to the right, lowering your hips and bending your knees to perform a lateral lunge.
As you lunge, simultaneously rotate your torso to the right and extend the weighted object away from your body.
Return to the starting position by stepping your right foot back to center, then repeat the sequence on the left side.
Continue to alternate between lateral lunges to the right and left, maintaining a controlled, circular movement pattern.

1725.description: The Weighted Bosu Ball Push-Up is a challenging upper body and core exercise that engages multiple muscle groups. It improves strength, stability, and balance by incorporating an unstable Bosu ball surface during the push-up motion.
instructions: Position a Bosu ball on the floor with the dome-side down, creating an unstable surface.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate against your chest, engaging your core.
Assume a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your feet positioned on the Bosu ball.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor, maintaining a straight body line from head to heels.
Press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

1943.description: The weighted box step squat is a compound exercise that targets the major lower body muscle groups, such as the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core. It combines the benefits of a traditional squat with the addition of a step-up motion, challenging stability and coordination.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or step with a dumbbell or kettlebell held at chest height.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you step up onto the box with one foot, followed by the other.
Descend back down by stepping back with the same foot you stepped up with, followed by the other foot, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat the sequence, alternating the lead foot with each repetition.

1275.description: The Weighted Bridge with Leg Extension is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the glutes, hamstrings, and core. This exercise helps to improve lower body strength, stability, and hip mobility.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your hips.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Extend one leg straight up toward the ceiling, keeping your hips and torso stable.
Slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position and repeat with the other leg.
Maintain the bridge position throughout the movement, making sure to keep your core engaged and your hips elevated.

1969.description: The Weighted Burpee is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the arms, chest, shoulders, core, and legs. This exercise challenges your strength, cardiovascular endurance, and overall body coordination.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight (dumbbell or kettlebell) at chest level.
Bend at the hips and knees to perform a squat, lowering the weight towards the ground.
Kick your feet back into a plank position, keeping your core engaged and your body in a straight line.
Perform a push-up, lowering your chest to the ground.
Explosively drive through your palms to return to the plank position, then jump your feet back towards your hands.
Stand up, engaging your glutes and core, and press the weight overhead.
Lower the weight back to the starting position at chest level and repeat.

1970.description: The Weighted Burpee Box Jump is a compound exercise that combines a burpee with a box jump, adding a weight vest or dumbbell to increase resistance and challenge the full-body musculature.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench with a weight vest or dumbbell held at chest level.
Squat down, placing your hands on the floor in front of you, and kick your feet back to assume a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then jump your feet back towards your hands, stand up, and explosively jump up onto the box.
Step or jump back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1672.description: The Weighted Burpee Pull Up is a compound exercise that combines the explosive power of a burpee with the upper body strength of a pull-up, making it an excellent choice for building overall strength and conditioning.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you, then kick your feet back to assume a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then immediately jump your feet back towards your hands and stand up, explosively driving through your heels.
Leap up, reaching the weight overhead, and perform a pull-up, pulling your chin over the bar.

1879.description: The Weighted Butterfly Situp is a challenging core exercise that targets multiple muscle groups simultaneously. It combines the benefits of a traditional situp with the added resistance of holding a weight between the feet, enhancing muscular strength and endurance.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet touching, creating a butterfly position.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, between your feet, engaging your core to keep the weight stable.
Keeping your arms extended, engage your abdominal muscles and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, performing a situp motion.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1050.description: The Weighted Cardio Core Crawl is a dynamic full-body exercise that combines cardio and core engagement. It targets various muscle groups while elevating the heart rate for an effective calorie-burning workout.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate between your feet, engaging your core to stabilize your body.
Keeping your core tight, crawl forward by alternately moving your hands and feet, maintaining the high plank position throughout the movement.
Move forward for the desired distance or duration, then reverse the movement to return to the starting position.

1673.description: The Weighted Chin Up is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups in the upper body, including the biceps, back, and shoulder muscles. This exercise can help build strength and muscular endurance.
instructions: Secure a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet or place it on your lap.
Grip the pull-up bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Pull your shoulder blades together, engage your core, and initiate the movement by pulling your elbows back and up, bringing your chin over the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.

1276.description: The Weighted Clam Bridge is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, core, and hip muscles. It engages the posterior chain while also challenging stability and balance.
instructions: Lie on your side with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place a dumbbell, weight plate, or other weight between your knees.
Engage your core and glutes, then raise your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold the bridge position for 2-3 seconds, ensuring your hips remain lifted and the weight is securely positioned between your knees.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps. Complete all sets on one side before switching to the other.

1726.description: The Weighted Clapping Push-Up is an advanced upper body strength exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It combines the traditional push-up with explosive clapping for increased power and muscle activation.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Explosively push yourself up, straightening your arms and lifting your hands off the floor to perform a clap.
Immediately lower your body back down in a controlled motion until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the movement.

1674.description: The Weighted Close Grip Chin-Up is a compound exercise that targets the biceps, back, and grip muscles. It helps to build upper body strength and muscle mass.
instructions: Attach a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet using a dip belt or towel.
Grab a chin-up bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, keeping your palms facing you.
Engage your core, pull your shoulder blades together, and initiate the movement by driving your elbows back to pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control.

1727.description: The Weighted Close Grip Medicine Ball Push Up is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps while also engaging the core musculature. This exercise challenges stability and recruits additional muscle fibers compared to a standard push-up.
instructions: Assume a standard push-up position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart and a medicine ball positioned between your hands.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Keeping your elbows tucked close to your body, lower your chest towards the medicine ball in a controlled motion.
Press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms while maintaining the tight core position.

1728.description: The Weighted Close Hands Push-Up is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. This variation increases the resistance and challenges the upper body stabilizers.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands placed slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart, your core engaged, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell between your hands, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower your chest towards the ground, maintaining control and keeping your elbows tucked.
Once your chest nearly touches the ground, press back up to the starting position by straightening your arms, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.

1111.description: The Weighted Crescent Circle is a full-body strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It involves a controlled circular motion while holding a weight, challenging stability and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, core engaged, and hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Initiate the movement by extending your arms out to the side, keeping the weight close to your body.
Slowly lower the weight towards the floor in a controlled circular motion, bending at the hips and knees as needed.
Once the weight reaches the floor, reverse the motion by extending your hips and knees to return to the starting position.

1564.description: The Weighted Cross Body Mountain Climber is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It challenges stability and coordination while also building strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height.
Engage your core and assume a high plank position, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Drive your opposite knee towards your chest, simultaneously reaching the dumbbell across your body towards the opposite knee.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, alternating sides with each repetition.

1085.description: The Weighted Cross Chop to Knee is a full-body exercise that engages the core, shoulders, and legs. It combines a diagonal chopping motion with a knee drive to improve coordination, stability, and functional strength.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands at chest level.
Initiate the movement by driving the weight diagonally across your body, extending your arms and rotating your torso to the opposite side.
As you chop the weight, simultaneously drive your opposite knee up towards your chest, engaging your core and leg muscles.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then return to the starting position in a controlled motion.

1640.description: The Weighted Cross Knee Strike is a plyometric exercise that challenges full-body coordination and explosiveness. This movement combines a lateral jump with a powerful knee strike, engaging the leg, core, and upper body muscles.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a weight plate or dumbbell at chest height.
Explosively jump to the left, driving your right knee up and across your body, simultaneously swinging the weight diagonally across your torso.
Land softly on your left foot, immediately driving back to the starting position with an explosive right jump, repeating the knee strike on the opposite side.
Maintain upright posture and core engagement throughout the movement, keeping the weight close to your body.

1167.description: The Weighted Cross Leg Reverse Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. It involves pulling the knees towards the chest while keeping the legs crossed, adding resistance with a dumbbell or weight plate for an increased challenge.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and a dumbbell or weight plate held between your feet.
Cross your legs at the ankles and engage your core to lift your hips off the floor, keeping your back flat against the ground.
Exhale as you pull your knees towards your chest, contracting your abdominal muscles.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position.

1881.description: The Weighted Cross Punch Roll Up is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups while improving core stability and upper body strength. It combines a cross-body punch with a controlled roll-up motion to challenge the abdominal, shoulder, and chest muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a light weight (such as a dumbbell or kettlebell) in one hand at chest height.
Brace your core and slowly punch the weight across your body, extending your arm fully.
Keeping your core engaged, initiate a controlled roll-up motion by lifting your shoulder blades off the floor, peeling your back off the ground one vertebra at a time.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1166.description: The Weighted Crossed Arms Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves crunching up while holding a weight plate or dumbbell against the chest, providing added resistance and intensity.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest, crossing your arms over it.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lift your shoulder blades off the floor, performing a controlled crunch.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1880.description: The Weighted Crossed Arms Sit Up is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves performing a sit-up motion while holding a weight plate or dumbbell across the chest, which increases the resistance and challenge.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, holding a weight plate or dumbbell across your chest with your arms crossed.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lower your back towards the floor, keeping your head, shoulders, and upper back off the ground.
Once your back almost touches the floor, pause briefly, then use your abdominal muscles to pull yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1675.description: The Weighted Crossover Chin-Up is a compound exercise that targets the back, biceps, and grip muscles. This variation incorporates a weighted plate or dumbbell held between the feet to increase resistance and challenge the user's strength and stability.
instructions: Attach a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet, ensuring it is secured in place.
Grip the pull-up bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, palms facing you.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades together as you initiate the movement by pulling your body up until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly lower yourself back down with control, keeping your body in a straight line throughout the exercise.

1168.description: The Weighted Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves using a weighted object to increase resistance and challenge the core during a traditional crunch movement.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell or weight plate against your chest.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and slowly curl your shoulders off the floor, lifting your shoulder blades slightly.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.

1169.description: The Weighted Crunch Chop is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the obliques, rectus abdominis, and transverse abdominis muscles. It combines a crunch motion with a rotational chop movement to challenge the midsection from multiple angles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a weight plate, dumbbell, or medicine ball with both hands at chest height.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back, keeping your core engaged. As you lower, rotate your torso to the right, bringing the weight towards the outside of your right hip.
Exhale and use your obliques to pull your torso back up to the starting position, rotating to the center as you rise.
Repeat the movement, this time lowering to the left side and rotating the weight towards your left hip.

1112.description: The Weighted Cycling Russian Twist is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It helps improve rotational stability and power generation.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, with both hands at chest level.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, maintaining a straight spine. Keep your feet on the floor throughout the movement.
Slowly twist your torso to the right, allowing the weight to move across your body. Pause briefly, then twist to the left in a controlled motion.
Continue alternating between right and left, keeping your movement controlled and your core engaged. Avoid swinging the weight or allowing your torso to rock back and forth.

1312.description: The Weighted Dead Bug is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and lower back. It challenges core stability and promotes better movement patterns.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead and your legs raised with knees bent at 90 degrees.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest, keeping your core engaged.
Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg towards the floor, keeping your back flat against the ground.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, alternating sides with each repetition.

1729.description: The Weighted Decline Push-Up is a challenging upper body exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It adds an additional level of resistance to the traditional push-up, enhancing muscular strength and endurance.
instructions: Position a weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, on the upper back, just below the neck.
Assume a push-up position with your feet elevated on a bench or platform, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower body to maintain a stable position throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor, bending at the elbows and keeping them close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the ground, press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

1641.description: The Weighted Depth Jump is a plyometric exercise that involves jumping down from a raised platform and immediately rebounding upward, engaging the major muscle groups of the lower body to develop explosive power and reactive strength.
instructions: Stand on a raised platform or box with a dumbbell held at chest height.
Initiate the movement by hinging at the hips and knees to lower your body into a quarter squat position.
Explosively drive through your heels to jump vertically off the platform, extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, immediately initiating the next repetition with a powerful rebound jump.

1730.description: The Weighted Diamond Push-Up is a challenging variation of the classic push-up that engages the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It requires stabilization and control throughout the movement, making it an excellent exercise for improving overall upper body strength.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands placed directly beneath your shoulders and your fingers pointing inward, forming a diamond shape.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other suitable weight on your upper back, just below your neck, to add resistance to the movement.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your body by bending at the elbows until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Pause briefly, then push back up to the starting position by straightening your arms, being mindful to maintain proper form throughout the movement.

1997.description: The Weighted Dip is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles, providing an effective upper body strength-building workout.
instructions: Stand between two parallel bars or dip stations, gripping them at shoulder-width.
Engage your core and straighten your arms to lift your body off the floor, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower your body until your elbows form 90-degree angles, then press back up to the starting position.
Throughout the movement, maintain a straight body position, avoiding arching your back or swinging your legs.

1033.description: The Weighted Donkey Calf Raise is a compound exercise that primarily targets the calf muscles, particularly the gastrocnemius and soleus. This exercise can help build strength, power, and muscle definition in the lower legs.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight (such as a dumbbell or kettlebell) between your thighs.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you bend at the hips to lower your torso, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Press through your heels to raise your body back to the starting position, contracting your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower back down, controlling the descent, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1170.description: The Weighted Double Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. This variation of the standard crunch adds resistance to challenge the abdominal muscles and improve overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button in towards your spine.
Curl your shoulders up off the floor, lifting the weight towards the ceiling while simultaneously lifting your hips off the floor to form a 'V' shape with your body.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position, being sure to keep the weight close to your chest throughout the movement.

1051.description: The weighted double under is a high-intensity cardio exercise that involves jumping rope while holding a weight in each hand. This exercise engages the entire body and can improve cardiovascular endurance, coordination, and agility.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand at your sides with palms facing inward.
Keep your core engaged and maintain good posture throughout the movement.
Swing the rope under your feet twice for each jump, ensuring the rope passes under your feet during each repetition.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, keeping your knees slightly bent to absorb the impact.

1565.description: The Weighted Elbow Plank Pike Jacks is a challenging core and shoulder exercise that works the abdominal muscles, shoulders, and triceps. This exercise requires balance, stability, and strength to execute properly.
instructions: Assume a plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from heels to head.
Engage your core and lift your hips up and back, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body.
Explosively pike your hips up and down, maintaining a straight line from heels to head throughout the movement.
Keep your arms extended and your shoulders stacked over your elbows as you pike up and down.

1171.description: The Weighted Elbow to Knee Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It helps improve overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a weight (such as a dumbbell or medicine ball) at your chest.
Engage your core and curl your upper body off the floor, bringing your right elbow towards your left knee.
Slowly lower back down and repeat on the other side, bringing your left elbow towards your right knee.
Alternate sides, keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.

1782.description: The Weighted Elevated Feet Inverted Row is a challenging strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the back, biceps, and core. It requires the use of body weight and an elevated surface to create an inverted pulling motion.
instructions: Position an elevated platform or sturdy table behind you, and place your feet on the surface with your legs extended.
Grip the edge of the platform with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and hang from your arms with your body in a straight line.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades together, bending your elbows, and bringing your chest up towards the platform.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control.

1566.description: The Weighted Elevated Feet Plank is a challenging core strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups throughout the body. By elevating the feet, it increases the demand on the abdominal muscles and requires greater stabilization.
instructions: Position a sturdy bench or box in front of you and place your feet on top, shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintain a neutral spine position.
Holding a dumbbell or weight plate across your chest, lower your body into a plank position, supporting your weight on your forearms and toes.
Hold this position, focusing on maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels, for the desired duration.

1113.description: The Weighted Elevated Feet Russian Twist is a core strengthening exercise that targets the obliques and other abdominal muscles. It helps improve rotation, stability, and overall core strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet elevated on a bench or box.
Hold a weight plate, dumbbell, or medicine ball in front of your chest with your arms extended.
Engage your core and slowly twist your torso from side to side, keeping your upper body stationary.
Control the movement and avoid swinging the weight. Exhale as you twist to each side.

1944.description: The Weighted Elevated Single Leg Squat is a compound exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles, while also challenging balance and stability.
instructions: Stand facing a bench or step with one foot elevated on the surface behind you.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in the hand opposite your elevated leg.
Keeping your torso upright, bend at the hip and knee to lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.
Pause briefly, then drive through your front heel to return to the starting position.

1567.description: The Weighted Elevator Abs exercise is a core-focused exercise that targets multiple abdominal muscles through controlled, weighted hip raises. This exercise helps to strengthen the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a weight plate or dumbbell securely between your feet.
Engage your core and slowly raise your hips up, lifting the weight off the floor while keeping your back straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring that you maintain control and engage your abdominal muscles throughout the exercise.

1731.description: The Weighted Explosive Crossover Push-Up is a dynamic exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and core. It combines the benefits of push-ups with an explosive, twisting motion to improve overall strength, power, and stability.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and a weight, such as a dumbbell or weight plate, placed between your hands.
Explosively push yourself up, lifting the weight off the ground and rotating your body to one side, twisting your chest and hips to face the opposite direction.
Control the descent back to the starting position, keeping the weight close to your body.
Repeat the explosive push-up and rotation on the opposite side, alternating sides with each repetition.

1732.description: The Weighted Explosive Push-Up is a challenging strength and power exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It involves performing explosive push-ups while holding a weight plate, plate, or medicine ball on the back.
instructions: Assume a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your core engaged.
Position a weight plate, plate, or medicine ball on your upper back, just below your neck.
Inhale and lower your body until your chest nearly touches the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Explosively press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms and lifting your hands off the ground momentarily to demonstrate power.

1568.description: The Weighted Extended Plank is a challenging core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups throughout the body. This variation of the traditional plank position adds resistance by having the individual hold a weight plate or dumbbell between their feet, requiring greater stabilization and engagement of the abdominal, back, and shoulder muscles.
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by drawing your navel in towards your spine and tightening your glutes and leg muscles.
Lift one foot off the floor and hold a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet, keeping your legs extended and your body in a straight line.
Hold this position, maintaining good form and keeping your core braced, for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
Slowly lower the weight back to the floor, then repeat with the opposite foot lifted.
Ensure that your hips do not sag or rise during the exercise, and keep your gaze slightly forward to maintain a neutral neck position.
Breathe normally throughout the exercise, avoiding holding your breath.

1313.description: The Weighted External Hip Raise targets the gluteal muscles, improving hip strength and stability. This exercise can be particularly beneficial for athletes and individuals seeking to enhance their lower body power and performance.
instructions: Lie on your side with your body in a straight line, supporting your head with your bottom hand.
Bend your top leg and place your foot flat on the floor in front of your body, keeping your bottom leg straight.
Place a weight (such as a dumbbell or kettlebell) on your top thigh, just above your knee.
Engage your core and gluteal muscles, then lift your top leg up towards the ceiling, keeping your knee in line with your body.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment, then slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position.

1733.description: The Weighted Feet Elevated Side to Side Push-up is a challenging full-body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps, while also engaging the core for stabilization.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your feet elevated on a bench or other stable surface, and hold a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your body down by bending your elbows to perform a push-up.
As you push back up, shift your body to the side, moving your hips and shoulders in one fluid motion.
Repeat the push-up and side shift on the other side, continuing to alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.

1945.description: The Weighted Figure Four Squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the glutes, quadriceps, and core, while also challenging balance and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in front of your chest.
Cross your right ankle over your left thigh, keeping your right knee pointing outward.
Engage your core and sit your hips back, lowering your body into a squat position while maintaining a straight back.
Press through your left heel to return to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.

1314.description: The Weighted Fire Hydrant Kick is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups in the hips, glutes, and core. It involves lifting one leg out to the side while holding a weight, creating resistance and engaging multiple muscle groups.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a dumbbell or other weight near your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift the opposite leg out to the side, keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold the lifted leg position for a moment, then lower it back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch sides.

1830.description: The Weighted Floor I Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, hips, and legs. It helps improve stability, balance, and overall lower body strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell between your hands.
Engage your core and slowly raise your arms, torso, and legs off the floor, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body.
Hold the raised position for a moment, focusing on squeezing your glutes and engaging your core.
Slowly lower your arms, torso, and legs back to the starting position in a controlled motion.

1807.description: The Weighted Floor Inverted Shoulder Press is a compound exercise that targets the deltoids, triceps, and core muscles. It helps build shoulder and arm strength while also engaging the stabilizing muscles of the torso.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your back flat and knees bent, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in both hands directly overhead with straight arms.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly lower the weight behind your head until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly, then press the weight back up over your chest with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the movement.

1831.description: The Weighted Floor T Raise is a strength-training exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and back. It helps improve upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Lie on the floor with a weight plate held at chest level, arms extended and palms facing each other.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly raise your arms out to the sides until they are in line with your shoulders, forming a 'T' shape with your body.
Hold the T position for a moment, then slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1832.description: The Weighted Floor Y Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups throughout the upper body and core. It challenges shoulder stability and promotes overall upper body strength.
instructions: Lie face-down on the floor with your arms extended in a 'Y' position, palms facing down and a dumbbell held between your hands.
Engage your core and slowly raise your arms and upper body off the floor, keeping your body in a straight line from heels to head.
Hold the top position for a brief pause, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1172.description: The Weighted Flutter Kicks is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, hip flexors, and quadriceps. It involves performing flutter kicks while holding a weight between the feet to increase resistance and challenge the core musculature.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and a weight (such as a dumbbell or medicine ball) held firmly between your ankles.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and lift your legs a few inches off the ground, keeping them straight.
Perform a flutter kick motion, alternating between raising your right and left leg while maintaining control and stability.
Keep your movements small and controlled, avoiding excessive range of motion or momentum.
Breathe evenly throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lower your legs and inhaling as you raise them.

1173.description: The Weighted Foam Roller Reverse Crunch On Bench is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves lifting the hips and lower back off a bench using a foam roller for support and added resistance.
instructions: Lie on a bench with your upper back and shoulders supported, holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your abdomen.
Place a foam roller under your lower back and extend your legs straight out.
Engage your core and lift your hips and lower back off the bench, curling your body towards the ceiling.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1277.description: The Weighted Front Kick Tabletop is a strength-building exercise that engages various muscle groups by combining a front kick with a tabletop position, adding resistance with a weight held in the kicking leg.
instructions: Start in a tabletop position on the floor, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Hold a light dumbbell or weight plate in your right hand and extend your right leg behind you, keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
Engaging your core, kick your right leg forward, extending your leg fully while maintaining the tabletop position.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position, keeping the weight held in your hand throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the same movement with your left leg.

1642.description: The Weighted Front Knee Strike is a plyometric exercise that develops explosive power in the lower body. This exercise mimics the striking motion of a front knee strike while incorporating a weighted object to increase resistance and challenge the muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball or other weighted object at chest level.
Initiate the movement by driving your front knee forcefully upward, straightening your leg and extending through the hips.
As you drive your knee up, explosively extend your arms to press the weighted object straight out in front of you.
Controlled lower the leg and the weighted object back to the starting position in a fluid motion.

1569.description: The Weighted Full Plank Passe Twist is a challenging core and stability exercise that engages multiple muscle groups. It helps improve overall core strength, balance, and functional movement patterns.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and glutes. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your lower back.
Keeping your core braced, slowly rotate your torso to the right, bringing your right shoulder towards the ground. Return to the starting position and repeat on the left side.
Maintain a stable, straight-line position throughout the movement, avoiding any sagging or arching in your lower back.

1882.description: The Weighted Get Up Sit Up is a compound exercise that strengthens the core, shoulder, and leg muscles. It involves getting up from a seated position while holding a weight, providing a challenging full-body workout.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell, kettlebell, or other weight at chest level with both hands.
Sit on the floor with your legs extended and the weight held at your chest.
Keeping the weight close to your body, use your core muscles to roll back and lie down on the floor.
Engage your core and leg muscles to push yourself back up to a seated position, maintaining control of the weight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1114.description: The weighted GHD back extension is a compound exercise that targets the muscles of the lower back and glutes. It helps to improve spinal and core stability, as well as overall strength and muscle development in the posterior chain.
instructions: Adjust the GHD (Glute-Ham Developer) machine to the appropriate height, ensuring your thighs are securely positioned under the leg pads.
Hold a weighted plate or dumbbell behind your head, keeping your arms extended.
Engage your core and slowly lower your torso towards the floor, maintaining a neutral spine position.
Once you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, pause briefly, then use your lower back and glute muscles to raise your torso back to the starting position.

1086.description: The Weighted Half Kneeling Rotation is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and hips. It improves rotational strength, stability, and mobility while also engaging the lower body.
instructions: Stand with one knee on the floor and the other foot flat on the ground, holding a dumbbell or other weight at shoulder height with both hands.
Engage your core and keep your torso upright as you slowly rotate your upper body to one side, keeping your hips stationary.
Pause briefly at the end of the rotation, then reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation on the same side for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the same number of reps.

1735.description: The Weighted Hand Release Push Up is a challenging variation of the classic push-up that engages the chest, shoulders, and triceps while also testing core stability. This exercise requires controlled movement and optimal form to safely execute.
instructions: Assume a standard push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or weight plate in each hand.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, then press back up to the starting position.
At the top of the movement, fully extend your arms and briefly release your hands from the weights, maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Grasp the weights again and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1734.description: The Weighted Handstand Push-Up is an advanced upper body strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the shoulders, chest, and triceps, while also challenging core stability and balance.
instructions: Set up facing a wall or other sturdy surface that can support your feet during the handstand position.
Kick up into a handstand, with your feet pressing against the wall for support and your body forming a straight line from heels to head.
Slowly lower your body by bending at the elbows, keeping your core engaged and your body rigid throughout the movement.
Once your head nearly touches the floor, pause briefly, then push back up to the starting handstand position, extending your arms fully.

1676.description: The Weighted Hanging Hurdle is a compound exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the back, shoulders, and core. It improves overall strength, stability, and grip strength.
instructions: Securely grip a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands.
Hang from a pull-up bar with arms extended, keeping the weight plate or dumbbell close to your chest.
Maintaining a controlled, slow pace, raise your knees towards your chest, lifting the weight plate or dumbbell with you.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, keeping the weight plate or dumbbell close to your body throughout the movement.

1416.description: The Weighted Hanging Knee Raise is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, hip flexors, and grip strength. It is an effective exercise for building core stability and overall upper body strength.
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your body straight, engage your core and lift your knees up towards your chest, bringing your thighs parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring to maintain good form throughout the exercise.

1174.description: The Weighted Hanging Knee Raise Oblique Crunch is a compound exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques, while also engaging the hip flexors and core stabilizers. This exercise challenges both strength and stability.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar or other sturdy overhead structure with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Engage your core and slowly raise your knees towards your chest, keeping your legs together.
At the top of the movement, crunch your torso to the right, bringing your right elbow towards your left knee.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side, crunching your torso to the left and bringing your left elbow towards your right knee.
Exhale as you crunch and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain control and focus on engaging your obliques throughout the movement.
For added challenge, hold a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet during the knee raises.

1417.description: The Weighted Hanging Leg Raise is a core strength exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves lifting the legs while suspended, challenging the core to stabilize the body.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly raise your straight legs up in front of you, keeping them together and aiming to bring them parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.

1418.description: The Weighted Hanging Single Leg Raise is an advanced core and leg exercise that challenges your abdominal strength, hip flexor mobility, and lower body stability.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar or other secure overhead support with an overhand grip, arms extended.
Keeping one leg straight, slowly raise that leg up towards the ceiling, contracting your abdominal muscles.
Hold the top position for a brief pause, then lower your leg back to the starting position in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1643.description: The Weighted High Box Jump is a plyometric exercise that develops explosive power, muscular strength, and coordination. This exercise involves jumping up onto a high box or platform while holding a weight, typically a dumbbell or kettlebell, which challenges the muscles to produce a greater force output.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box or platform that is approximately knee to hip height.
Grip a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest, keeping your core engaged.
Initiate the movement by bending your hips and knees to lower your body, maintaining a flat back and keeping your chest up.
Explosively drive through your heels to jump up onto the box, fully extending your hips and knees.
Land softly on the box, controlling the weight and maintaining your balance.
Step or jump back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1315.description: The Weighted Hip Circles exercise targets various lower body muscles and helps improve hip mobility, stability, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight at chest level with both hands.
Keeping your back straight and core engaged, slowly circle your hips in a clockwise direction, maintaining control of the weight throughout the movement.
Perform 10-15 clockwise circles, then reverse the direction and complete 10-15 counter-clockwise circles.
Ensure your hips are leading the movement, not your shoulders or upper body.

1175.description: The Weighted Hip Crossover is a strength-based exercise that targets various muscle groups by incorporating a controlled hip rotation and lateral movement. This exercise can help improve core stability, hip mobility, and overall body coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and a weight plate or dumbbell held at chest level.
Keeping your core engaged, initiate a controlled hip rotation to the left, crossing your left leg in front of your right.
Return to the starting position by rotating your hips back to the center, then repeat the movement to the right, crossing your right leg in front of your left.
Maintain a stable upper body throughout the exercise, avoiding excessive movement in the torso.

1278.description: The Weighted Hip Extension and Cross exercise is a compound strength-training movement that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back muscles while also engaging the core for stability. This exercise helps to improve hip mobility, posture, and overall lower body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Keeping your back straight, hinge at the hips to lower your torso towards the floor, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
As you return to standing, rotate your torso to the right, bringing the weight across your body.
Repeat the movement, rotating to the left on the way back to the starting position.

1279.description: The weighted hip raise is a strength-building exercise that primarily targets the glutes and hamstrings. It involves lifting the hips off the floor while holding a weight on the lower abdomen, challenging the posterior chain muscles.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your lower abdomen, just below your navel.
Engage your core and gluteal muscles, then press through your heels to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold the top position for a brief pause, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring to keep your core braced and maintain good form throughout the movement.

1280.description: The Weighted Hip Raise with Feet on Swiss Ball is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It challenges stability and coordination while strengthening the posterior chain.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and place your shoulder blades and upper back on the ball, keeping your feet hip-width apart.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell securely on your hips or across your abdomen.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.

1281.description: The Weighted Hip Raise with Head on BOSU Ball is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It helps to improve hip mobility, strength, and stability.
instructions: Sit on the BOSU ball with your shoulders, head, and upper back resting on the platform. Engage your core and keep your feet shoulder-width apart, with knees bent at 90 degrees.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate securely on your hips or at your chest, keeping your arms extended.
Inhale and press your heels into the floor, driving through your heels to lift your hips up towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1282.description: The Weighted Hip Raise with Head on Swiss Ball is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. This exercise enhances hip extension strength and stability while also challenging your balance.
instructions: Lie with your shoulders and head resting on a Swiss ball, your legs extended, and a weight plate held on your hips.
Engage your core and gluteal muscles, then lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for 2 seconds, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring your movements are controlled and your core remains braced throughout the exercise.

1283.description: The Weighted Hip Raise with Knee Squeeze is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles, helping to improve hip and core stability, as well as overall lower body strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your hips.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor, pressing through your heels.
At the top of the movement, squeeze your knees together while maintaining a neutral spine.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position, being careful to control the descent.

1353.description: The Weighted Hollow Hold and Roll is a challenging core and full-body exercise that strengthens the abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and shoulder stabilizers while also improving body control and stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead and legs straight, engaging your core to lift your shoulders, arms, and legs off the floor in a hollow body position.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest, keeping your core braced and body in a straight line.
Slowly lower your arms and legs towards the floor, then use your abdominal muscles to roll back up to the starting hollow hold position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining tension in your core throughout the movement.

1176.description: The Weighted Hollow Rock is a core-strengthening exercise that challenges the entire body to maintain a stable, hollow position while rocking back and forth. This exercise develops abdominal bracing, shoulder stability, and full-body tension.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead and your legs straight, keeping your body in a hollow, rounded shape.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button in towards your spine and squeezing your glutes.
Holding a weight plate, dumbbell, or other weighted object against your chest, slowly rock your body back and forth, keeping your limbs and torso in a straight line.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding sagging in the middle or arching your back.

1883.description: The Weighted Hovering Sit-Up is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves holding a weight plate or dumbbell against the chest while performing a sit-up motion, challenging the core stabilizers throughout the movement.
instructions: Start by sitting on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell firmly against your chest.
Engage your core by bracing your abdominal muscles and keeping your back straight.
Slowly lower your torso towards the floor, maintaining control and keeping the weight plate or dumbbell pressed against your chest.
Once your upper back touches the floor, pause briefly, then use your abdominal muscles to lift your torso back to the starting position.

1570.description: The Weighted Inching Elbow Plank is a challenging core exercise that engages multiple muscle groups while improving stability and strength. By adding weight and gradually inching the body forward, this variation of the traditional plank exercise increases the demand on the muscles.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, engaging your core and glutes.
Place a dumbbell, weight plate, or other weight in front of your body within arm's reach.
Keeping your body in a straight line, slowly reach the weight with one hand, moving your body forward in a controlled manner.
Once you've moved the weight, return to the starting position and repeat the movement with the other hand, inching your body forward.
Continue alternating hands, moving the weight and your body forward in a smooth, controlled motion.
Maintain proper form throughout the exercise, keeping your core braced and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Perform for the desired number of repetitions or time, then carefully return to the starting position.

1571.description: The Weighted Inchworm to Side Plank is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and upper body. It combines a weighted inchworm movement with a side plank, challenging stability and total-body strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hips to lower your torso, keeping your back flat as you walk your hands out to a high plank position, maintaining the weight in your hands.
Carefully walk your feet towards your hands, keeping your core engaged and your body in a straight line.
Once your feet meet your hands, immediately rotate your body to the side, stacking your feet and placing your top hand on the floor, entering a side plank position.
Hold the side plank for 2-3 seconds, then return to the high plank position and repeat the inchworm motion, alternating sides with each rep.

1998.description: The Weighted Incline Dip is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It enhances upper body pushing strength and stability by adding weight to the traditional dip movement performed on an incline bench.
instructions: Position an incline bench at a 45-degree angle. Grip the dip bars with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, straighten your back, and extend your legs in front of you, crossing your ankles for stability.
Initiate the movement by bending at the elbows and lowering your body until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press through the palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position, fully extending your elbows.

1833.description: The Weighted Incline I Raise targets various muscle groups and is a great exercise for improving overall upper body strength and stability. It involves raising the arms while holding weights in an inclined position to engage the shoulders, chest, and back.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight in each hand with your palms facing inward.
Engage your core and tilt your torso forward at a 45-degree angle, keeping your back straight.
Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping them extended and in line with your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.

1834.description: The Weighted Incline L Raise is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves raising the legs while maintaining a fixed torso position, providing a challenging isometric contraction for the core.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, with your back supported and feet secured under the footrest.
Extend your arms out to your sides, palms down, to help stabilize your body.
Slowly raise your straight legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them in an 'L' shape with your thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back down, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on engaging your core muscles throughout the exercise.

1736.description: The Weighted Incline Push-Up is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It challenges the upper body's strength and stability while incorporating additional resistance for a more intense workout.
instructions: Adjust a bench or sturdy surface to a 30-45 degree incline.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other resistance on your upper back, just below the shoulders.
Assume a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly lower your chest towards the inclined surface, keeping your core engaged and elbows tucked close to your body.

1284.description: The Weighted Incline Rear Leg Extension is a strength-building exercise that targets the posterior chain, including the hamstrings and glutes. It involves extending the weighted leg while maintaining proper form and stability.
instructions: Stand facing an elevated surface like a bench or step, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Hinge at the hips to raise the weighted leg straight back, maintaining a neutral spine and engaging the core.
Slowly lower the leg back down, resisting the weight, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the process, ensuring to keep the torso stable throughout the movement.

1177.description: The Weighted Incline Reverse Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the rectus abdominis and obliques. It involves raising the legs while keeping the upper body stationary on an incline to increase resistance and engagement of the core.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench, holding a weight plate or dumbbell securely against your chest.
Extend your legs out in front of you, keeping them straight and together.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles, then slowly raise your legs towards the ceiling, lifting your hips off the bench.
Once your legs are perpendicular to the floor, pause briefly, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.

1835.description: The Weighted Incline T Raise is a compound exercise that targets the deltoids, upper back, and core muscles. It helps to build shoulder strength, improve posture, and enhance overall upper body stability.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 30-45 degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand with your palm facing down.
Lie on the incline bench with your chest and hips supported, extending your working arm straight up towards the ceiling.
Keeping your arm straight, raise the weight out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, squeezing your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps before switching sides.

1837.description: The Weighted Incline Y Raise is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the upper back, shoulders, and chest. It helps to improve overall upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Lean forward at the hips to create an incline, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Raise the weights out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your arms. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1316.description: The Weighted Inner Thigh Lift is a strength-based exercise that targets the inner thigh muscles, helping to tone and strengthen the lower body.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and a dumbbell or weight plate placed between your ankles.
Engage your core and lift your top leg, keeping your knees in line with your hips.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the same number of reps on the other leg.

1783.description: The Weighted Inverted Row With Feet On Swiss Ball is a compound exercise that primarily targets multiple muscle groups, including the back, shoulders, and arms, while also engaging the core. This exercise challenges stability and improves overall upper body strength.
instructions: Position a sturdy bar or suspension trainer at hip height and place a Swiss ball behind you.
Lie down with your feet on the Swiss ball and your hands gripping the bar with an overhand, slightly wider than shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your body in a straight line from heels to head, engage your core and pull your shoulder blades together to lift your body until your chest nearly touches the bar.
Slowly lower yourself back down with control until your arms are fully extended, then repeat.

1808.description: The Weighted Inverted Shoulder Press is a challenging upper body exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the deltoids, triceps, and core, while improving shoulder stability and pressing strength.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and extend your arm straight overhead, keeping the weight directly over your shoulder.
Slowly lower the weight behind your head, maintaining control and keeping your elbow close to your ear.
Once your forearm is parallel to the floor, press the weight back overhead to the starting position.

1644.description: The Weighted Isometric Explosive Jump Squat is a plyometric exercise that combines an isometric squat hold with a explosive jump, engaging multiple muscle groups and improving power output.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell or weight plate across the upper back.
Initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees, keeping the chest upright and core braced.
Descend until the thighs are parallel to the floor, hold this isometric position for 2-3 seconds.
Explosively drive through the heels to jump up, fully extending the hips and knees.
Land softly back in the starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps.

1737.description: The Weighted Isometric Explosive Push-Up is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps, while also developing explosive power and strength.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back, keeping your core engaged to maintain proper form.
Perform a push-up by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor, pausing briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Explosively push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms and engaging your chest and shoulders.

1738.description: The Weighted Judo Push-Up is a challenging compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps, while also engaging the core muscles for stability. It adds an extra resistance element to the traditional push-up by incorporating a weight plate or medicine ball.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and a weight plate or medicine ball positioned between your hands.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Slowly lower your body toward the floor, keeping your elbows close to your sides and your chest facing the ground.
Once your chest nearly touches the weight, pause briefly, then push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the movement.

1053.description: The Weighted Jump Rope is a cardio exercise that engages various muscle groups while elevating your heart rate. This exercise can help improve cardiovascular fitness, coordination, and agility.
instructions: Grasp the ends of the jump rope with your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Maintain an upright posture with your core engaged, and begin swinging the rope under your feet.
Jump lightly off the ground, clearing the rope as it passes beneath your feet.
Maintain a smooth, consistent rhythm, ensuring the rope passes under your feet with each jump.
Keep your movements controlled and your body tension engaged throughout the exercise.

1054.description: The Weighted Jump Rope Crossover is a cardio exercise that engages various muscle groups while improving coordination and agility. This exercise challenges the body by incorporating a weighted jump rope with a crossover movement pattern.
