instructions: Hold a weighted jump rope in both hands with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and core engaged.
Swing the rope behind your back, then cross it in front of your body, jumping as the rope passes under your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, maintaining control and balance throughout the movement.

1055.description: The Weighted Jump Rope Jog is a cardiovascular exercise that combines the benefits of jumping rope with the added resistance of a weighted rope. This exercise helps improve coordination, agility, and overall fitness.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the weighted jump rope in both hands in front of your body.
Swing the rope behind you and jump up, allowing the rope to pass beneath your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, maintaining a slight bend in the knees.
Continue jumping and swinging the rope, maintaining a steady, controlled pace.
Keep your core engaged and your movements fluid throughout the exercise.

1052.description: The Weighted Jumping Jacks exercise is a cardiovascular workout that engages multiple muscle groups and increases heart rate. It involves adding light weights to the traditional jumping jacks movement to enhance the overall intensity and calorie burn.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing inward.
Initiate the movement by jumping your feet out to the sides while simultaneously raising your arms out to the sides and overhead.
Immediately jump your feet back together while lowering your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat the jumping motion, alternating between the open and closed leg positions, while maintaining control of the weights.

1677.description: Weighted Jumping Pull-Ups are a challenging compound exercise that targets the upper body, core, and lower body muscles. This exercise combines a explosive jump with a pull-up motion, engaging multiple muscle groups for a comprehensive strength training workout.
instructions: Start by standing facing a sturdy pull-up bar, holding a weighted object (such as a dumbbell or kettlebell) between your feet.
Engage your core, bend your knees, and explosively jump up, extending your legs to lift the weight off the floor.
As you reach the top of the jump, immediately pull your body up towards the bar, performing a pull-up motion.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower your body back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the exercise.

1354.description: The Weighted Kicks exercise is a strength-building move that targets various muscle groups. It involves lifting one leg while holding a weight and performing a kicking motion, engaging the core and leg muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in one hand at your side.
Engage your core and lift the opposite leg, extending it out in front of you while keeping your knee slightly bent.
Swing the weighted leg forward, kicking the weight out in front of you, and then return your leg to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of reps, then switch sides and perform the exercise on the other leg.

1678.description: The Weighted Kipping Pull-Up is a challenging compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the back, shoulders, and arms, while also requiring core stability. It builds upper body strength and power.
instructions: Secure a weight (dumbbell or weight plate) between your feet or thighs, keeping your legs straight and together.
Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and initiate the movement by swinging your legs to generate momentum.
Pull yourself up explosively, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower yourself back down with control until your arms are fully extended, resisting the weight of the added resistance.

1356.description: The Weighted Knee Raises exercise targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, hip flexors, and quadriceps, to improve core strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell securely between your feet.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you slowly raise your knees toward your chest, lifting the weight off the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.

1115.description: The Weighted Kneeling Ab Wheel is a challenging core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles and develops overall core stability. It involves rolling out on an ab wheel while holding a weight plate or dumbbell to increase resistance and engagement.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and engage your core. Grasp an ab wheel with both hands and extend your arms to roll the wheel forward, lowering your chest towards the floor.
Maintain a straight body position, avoiding sagging in the hips or arching in the back. Grip a weight plate or dumbbell firmly against your chest throughout the movement.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then reverse the motion by engaging your abdominal muscles to roll the wheel back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and control throughout the exercise.

1178.description: The Weighted Kneeling Cross Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups by combining a crunch with a rotation. It helps improve overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lower your torso toward the floor, keeping your back straight.
As you lower down, twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight toward your right hip.
Pause briefly, then return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

1572.description: The Weighted Kneeling Plank is a variation of the traditional plank that challenges core stability and strength by adding resistance from a weight plate or dumbbell placed on the upper back.
instructions: Kneel on the floor, keeping your knees shoulder-width apart and your shins in contact with the ground.
Engage your core and extend your arms to support your body in a straight-arm plank position, with your hands positioned directly under your shoulders.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back, just below your neck, keeping your core braced and maintaining a neutral spine alignment.
Hold this position, focusing on keeping your body in a straight line from your knees to your head, for the desired duration.

1739.description: The Weighted Kneeling Push-Up is a challenging variation of the traditional push-up that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps while also engaging the core musculature to maintain stability in the kneeling position.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and your feet together behind you.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell securely against your chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Engage your core and lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, maintaining a straight line from your knees to your head.
Exhale as you push yourself back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

1573.description: The Weighted Kneeling Side Plank With Leg Lift is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and hips. It challenges stability and balance while building strength.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your right knee and foot on the ground, your left foot behind you, and your left elbow on the floor, arm extended.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from your knees to your head. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell on your left hip.
Slowly raise your left leg as high as you comfortably can, keeping your body in a straight line. Hold for a moment, then lower your leg back to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps, then switch sides and repeat the exercise on the other side.

1355.description: The Weighted Kneeling Superman is a core and back strengthening exercise that targets the muscles of the posterior chain. It involves extending the limbs while maintaining a braced core position, challenging stability and control.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your knees shoulder-width apart and your hands extended in front of you, holding a dumbbell or weight plate.
Engage your core muscles and maintain a neutral spine as you simultaneously raise your arms, chest, and legs off the floor, extending your limbs away from your body in a 'superman' position.
Hold this extended position for a 2-3 second count, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core braced and avoiding sagging or arching in the lower back.

1679.description: The Weighted L Pull Up is a challenging upper body exercise that primarily targets the lats, biceps, and core muscles. This variation of the traditional pull-up adds weight to increase resistance and difficulty, leading to greater strength and muscle development.
instructions: Start by securing a weight, such as a dumbbell or plate, between your feet or ankles.
Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and hang from the bar with your arms extended.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades together, contracting your lats, and pulling your body up until your chin is over the bar.
Hold the top position briefly, then slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining tension in your core and lower body throughout the exercise.

1645.description: The Weighted Lateral Leap and Hop is a plyometric exercise that targets multiple muscle groups and improves lateral power, agility, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a quarter squat position.
Explosively leap to the side, pushing through your feet to propel your body laterally.
Land softly on the opposite foot, immediately transitioning into a quick hop back to the starting position.
Repeat the sequence, alternating the direction of the leap and hop.

1646.description: The Weighted Lateral Plyo Squat is a plyometric exercise that targets multiple muscle groups while challenging lower body power and explosive movements. This exercise improves coordination, stability, and overall athletic performance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest height.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a squat position, keeping your chest up and core braced.
Explode upward and laterally, jumping your feet out to the side while extending your hips and knees.
Land softly with control, returning to the starting position and repeating on the opposite side.

1574.description: The Weighted Lateral Roll is a challenging core exercise that targets various stabilizing muscles while improving balance and coordination. It engages the obliques, transverse abdominis, and other core muscles to control the rotational movement of the torso.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Keeping your core braced, slowly lower your torso to the left, rolling your body as you shift your weight onto your left foot.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then use your core muscles to roll your body back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement to the right side, maintaining control throughout the exercise.

1647.description: The Weighted Lateral Slide is a plyometric exercise that challenges lateral power and coordination. It develops explosive strength and stability in the lower body while improving lateral movement patterns.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a weighted object (such as a dumbbell or medicine ball) at chest height.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and shifting your weight to one side, bending the hip and knee of the loaded leg.
Explosively drive through the loaded leg to slide your body laterally in the opposite direction, maintaining a stable core and upright torso throughout the movement.
Land softly on the opposite leg, immediately reversing the direction and sliding back to the starting position.
Repeat the lateral slides, alternating directions for the desired number of repetitions or time.

1419.description: The Weighted Lateral Stepover is a lower body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the glutes, quadriceps, and core, while also improving balance and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and step your left foot out to the side, followed by your right foot, creating a lateral step.
Engage your core and return to the starting position by stepping your right foot back to the center, followed by your left foot.
Repeat the lateral step to the other side, leading with the opposite foot.

1403.description: The Weighted Leg Curl is a strength-training exercise that targets the hamstring muscles, which are responsible for bending the knee. This exercise can help improve lower body strength, stability, and overall leg muscle development.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat surface with your legs straight and your ankles secured under a padded roller or weight plate.
Bend your knees and curl your heels towards your glutes, lifting your thighs off the floor and contracting your hamstrings.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring that your movements are controlled and your core remains engaged throughout the exercise.

1179.description: The Weighted Leg Extensions target the quadriceps muscles, helping to build strength and muscular endurance in the front of the thighs. This exercise can be performed with a dumbbell or resistance band for added resistance.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your back supported and your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell or resistance band between your ankles, keeping your legs extended and parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and slowly extend your legs, straightening your knees to lift the weight or band up towards the ceiling.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.

1420.description: The Weighted Leg Lowering Drill is a core strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the abdomen and lower body. It helps improve stability, balance, and overall core control.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms down.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles, and lift your legs straight up towards the ceiling.
Slowly lower your legs towards the floor, keeping your core braced and your back flat against the ground.
Pause briefly when your legs are a few inches above the floor, then return to the starting position by lifting your legs back up towards the ceiling.

1479.description: The Weighted Lunge is a lower-body strength exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It helps improve leg strength, balance, and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest level.
Take a large step forward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees form 90-degree angles.
Push back to the starting position with the front leg and repeat on the other side.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged throughout the movement.

1480.description: The Weighted Lunge Matrix is a comprehensive lower body strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups through a series of directional lunges while holding a weight. This exercise improves overall lower body strength, balance, and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Step forward with your right leg, lowering your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee nearly touches the floor. Push back to the starting position.
Step your right leg out to the side, lowering your body into a lateral lunge. Push back to the starting position.
Step your right leg back, lowering your body into a reverse lunge. Push back to the starting position.
Repeat the sequence on the left side, stepping forward, out to the side, and back with the left leg.
Continue alternating sides, completing the full lunge matrix on each leg.

1575.description: The Weighted Lying Reverse Plank is a full-body strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, back, and shoulders. This exercise helps improve overall stability, posture, and muscular endurance.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your legs extended and your arms extended behind you, palms flat on the floor.
Engage your core and lift your hips, shoulders, and knees off the floor, forming a straight line from your heels to your head.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate centered on your hips, keeping your body in a straight line.
Slowly lower your hips back to the floor, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1421.description: The Weighted Lying Straight Leg Raise is a challenging core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It helps to strengthen the hip flexors, lower back, and overall core stability.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and arms at your sides, palms down.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles.
Keeping your legs straight, slowly raise them towards the ceiling as high as you comfortably can, while keeping your lower back pressed into the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.

1285.description: The Weighted Marching Hip Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups in the lower body, core, and hips. It helps improve hip mobility, stability, and overall lower body strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell or other weight between your knees.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly raise your hips up, lifting the weight off the floor while maintaining a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Alternate raising your right and left legs as you march in place, maintaining control and stability throughout the exercise.

1286.description: The Weighted Marching Hip Raise With Feet on a Swiss Ball is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the glutes, hamstrings, and core. This exercise challenges stability and strength, providing a comprehensive lower body and core workout.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball against a wall and place your feet on top of the ball, shoulders-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate across your chest, keeping your arms extended.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Slowly lower your hips back down, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1180.description: The Weighted McGill Curl Up is an abdominal strengthening exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. It helps to improve core stability and muscular endurance.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and slowly curl your upper body off the floor, keeping your lower back in contact with the ground.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.

1576.description: The Weighted Medicine Ball Mountain Climber is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups simultaneously, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It challenges stability and dynamic strength while incorporating cardiovascular elements.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weighted medicine ball at your chest with both hands.
Engage your core and drive one knee up towards your chest, bringing your opposite elbow down to meet it.
Quickly switch legs, driving the opposite knee up and bringing the opposite elbow down.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion, keeping your body low and core engaged throughout the movement.

1740.description: The Weighted Medicine Ball Push-Up is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It combines the benefits of a traditional push-up with the added challenge of stabilizing a weighted medicine ball.
instructions: Place a weighted medicine ball on the floor in front of you.
Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the medicine ball, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1680.description: The Weighted Mixed Grip Chin Up is a compound pull-up exercise that targets the back, biceps, and grip strength. It involves pulling the body up to a bar with an overhand grip on one hand and an underhand grip on the other, adding weight to increase resistance and muscular development.
instructions: Attach a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet or use a weight belt around your waist.
Grip the bar with one hand in an overhand grip and the other hand in an underhand grip, hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, pull your shoulder blades together, and begin the movement by pulling your body up until your chin is over the bar.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, keeping your elbows close to your body throughout the movement.

1681.description: The Weighted Mixed Grip Pull-Up is a compound exercise that targets the back, biceps, and grip strength. It involves pulling your body up to a bar with one palm facing forward and the other facing backward, adding resistance with a weight plate or dumbbell.
instructions: Attach a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet or ankles using a strap or towel.
Grip the pull-up bar with one hand in an overhand grip and the other in an underhand grip, keeping your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, keeping your body in a straight line throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the hand positions and perform the same number of reps.

1116.description: The Weighted Modified Front Lever is a challenging core and upper body exercise that develops isometric strength, stability, and body control. It requires the athlete to hold a levered body position while supporting additional weight.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest using both hands.
Engage your core by bracing your abdominal muscles and tightening your glutes and hamstrings.
Lean your body back, extending your hips and maintaining a straight line from heels to head.
Hold the lever position, keeping your body rigid and resisting any sagging or bending at the hips or knees.

1784.description: The Weighted Modified Inverted Row is a compound exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the back, shoulders, and arms, while also engaging the core. This exercise is a variation of the traditional inverted row and can help build strength and muscular endurance.
instructions: Secure a sturdy bar or table at waist height and position yourself underneath it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades together, lifting your body until your chest nearly touches the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.

1577.description: The Weighted Modified Mountain Climber And Extension is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It combines the dynamics of a mountain climber with the stabilization of an extension, challenging the body's balance and coordination.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and raise one leg at a time, bringing your knee toward your chest in a mountain climber motion.
As you bring your knee in, press your opposite hand into the floor to extend your arm and rotate your torso, creating a side plank extension.
Alternate sides, maintaining control and stability throughout the movement.

1181.description: The Weighted Modified Pilates Roll Up With Ball is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It combines the rolling motion of a traditional Pilates roll-up with the added challenge of holding a weighted ball to engage the abdominal and back muscles.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, holding a weighted ball or dumbbell against your chest.
Slowly roll back, keeping your core engaged, until your shoulder blades touch the floor.
Pause briefly, then roll back up to the starting position in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping the ball pressed firmly against your chest throughout the movement.

1578.description: The Weighted Mountain Climber is a full-body strength exercise that engages multiple muscle groups simultaneously, including the core, shoulders, and legs. This exercise helps improve overall muscular endurance and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in front of your chest with both hands.
Engage your core and assume a high plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders.
Bring one knee up towards your chest, then quickly switch legs, alternating sides in a running motion.
Keep your hips low and your back flat throughout the movement. Maintain control and avoid swinging the weight.

1579.description: The Weighted Mountain Climber On Sliding Discs is a challenging full-body exercise that engages multiple muscle groups while incorporating dynamic, sliding movements. This exercise helps improve core strength, stability, and overall fitness.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your feet on sliding discs or towels.
Engage your core and drive one knee up toward your chest, sliding the foot back to the starting position.
Repeat with the opposite leg, alternating between legs in a running motion while keeping your hips low and your body in a straight line.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest to add resistance and further challenge your core and upper body.

1580.description: The Weighted Mountain Climber With Feet On Bosu Ball is a challenging full-body exercise that engages multiple muscle groups while improving balance, core strength, and cardiovascular endurance.
instructions: Position a Bosu ball with the flat side down on the floor and stand with your feet on top of it, shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands at chest level, engaging your core.
Maintaining a straight line from head to heels, drive one knee up towards your chest, then quickly switch legs, mimicking a running motion.
Continue alternating legs, keeping your hips low and your torso stable throughout the movement.

1581.description: The Weighted Mountain Climber With Hands On Swiss Ball is a challenging full-body exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It combines the benefits of a mountain climber with the instability of a Swiss ball to enhance core activation and overall strength.
instructions: Place a Swiss ball on the floor and position your hands on top of it, shoulder-width apart.
Assume a high plank position with your arms extended and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Keeping your core engaged, drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs, bringing the opposite knee in.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion while maintaining control and stability on the Swiss ball.

1021.description: The Weighted One Arm Floor Press is a strength-building exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It challenges core stability and shoulder mobility while building upper body pushing power.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your back flat, knees bent, and feet flat on the ground. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and extend your arm straight up toward the ceiling, keeping your elbow tucked close to your body.
Inhale as you slowly lower the weight toward your chest, maintaining control and keeping your elbow stationary.
Exhale as you press the weight back up to the starting position, fully extending your arm.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.

1741.description: The Weighted One Arm Push Up is a challenging upper body exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. By adding weight to one hand, this variation increases the demand on the working arm and core muscles.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands directly under your shoulders.
Place a weight, such as a dumbbell or plate, in one hand. Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbow, keeping it tucked close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the floor, push back up to the starting position by straightening your arm, focusing on contracting the chest, shoulder, and triceps of the working arm.
Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch and repeat on the other arm.

1117.description: The Weighted Open Knee Tucks is a strength-building exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the core, hips, and legs. It involves bringing the knees toward the chest while holding a weight between the feet.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight (e.g., medicine ball, dumbbell) between the feet.
Engage the core and bend at the hips to lower into a squat, keeping the back straight.
Explosively drive through the heels to extend the hips and bring the knees toward the chest, lifting the weight off the floor.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1742.description: The Weighted Parallette Handstand Push-Up is an advanced strength exercise that targets the shoulders, triceps, and core. This exercise improves upper body strength, balance, and stability.
instructions: Set up parallettes or sturdy push-up stands on the floor, ensuring they are stable and secure.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your back, positioned between your shoulder blades.
Kick up into a handstand position, with your feet elevated on the parallettes and your body in a straight line.
Slowly lower your body until your head nearly touches the floor, keeping your core engaged and your body straight.
Pause briefly, then push back up to the starting handstand position, fully extending your arms.

1946.description: The Weighted Partial Single Leg Squat is a variation of the traditional squat that targets the muscles of the lower body, particularly the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. This exercise challenges balance and stability while building lower body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height.
Shift your weight to one leg, keeping the other foot raised off the floor.
Initiate the movement by hinging at the hips and bending the standing knee to lower your body until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly, then drive through your heel to return to the starting position.

1182.description: The Weighted Pilates Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles while adding resistance to challenge the body. It helps improve overall core stability, muscular endurance, and spinal mobility.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell or other weight directly above your chest, arms extended.
Inhale as you slowly curl your upper back off the floor, engaging your abdominal muscles to lift the weight toward the ceiling.
Exhale as you lower back down to the starting position, maintaining control of the weight.

1183.description: The Weighted Pilates Roll Up With Ball is a core-strengthening exercise that engages the abdominal muscles while improving spinal mobility and flexibility.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and a weighted ball held at chest level.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly roll back onto your upper back, allowing your head and shoulders to gently lower towards the floor.
Pause briefly, then use your abdominal muscles to roll back up to the starting position, keeping the weighted ball at chest level throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the exercise.

1947.description: The Weighted Pistol Squat is a challenging single-leg exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes while also engaging the core for balance and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest.
Shift your weight onto your right leg, raising your left leg out in front of you with your knee bent and foot slightly off the ground.
Keeping your chest upright and core braced, lower your hips by bending your right knee to perform a controlled squat, ensuring your right knee tracks over your toes.
Press through your right heel to return to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.

945.description: The Weighted Plank targets the triceps, chest, shoulders, and abdominals. By adding a weight plate on the upper back, this variation increases the challenge and engagement of the core stabilizing muscles.
instructions: Assume a standard high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and engage your glutes and quads to maintain proper alignment.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other resistance on the middle of your upper back, just below the shoulder blades.
Hold the plank position, keeping your elbows stationary and your body rigid, for the desired duration.

1582.description: The Weighted Plank Jacks With Feet On Sliding Discs is a challenging core and full-body exercise that engages multiple muscle groups simultaneously. It combines the stability of a plank with the explosive movement of plank jacks, adding an extra challenge by placing the feet on sliding discs.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet on sliding discs or towels.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.
Explosively jump your feet out and back in, maintaining a tight plank position and keeping your hips level.
Hold a weight plate, dumbbell, or other object against your chest to add resistance and challenge your stabilizer muscles.
Perform the exercise for the desired number of repetitions or duration, ensuring you maintain proper form and control throughout.

1357.description: The Weighted Plank Knee Tucks is a compound exercise that works multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It challenges stability and strength while promoting full-body engagement.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your lower back.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and squeeze your glutes to maintain a neutral spine.
Keeping your core braced, bend your knees and bring them towards your chest, lifting your hips up towards the ceiling.
Pause briefly, then slowly return to the starting high plank position by extending your legs.

1583.description: The Weighted Plank Knee Twist is a full-body strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It challenges core stability and rotational control.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, core engaged, and body in a straight line from head to heels. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your lower back.
Keeping your core braced, slowly lower your right knee towards the floor, twisting your torso to the right. Return to the starting position and repeat on the left side.
Alternate sides, moving your knees towards the floor and twisting your torso in the opposite direction. Maintain a steady, controlled pace throughout the movement.
Ensure your hips remain square and do not sag or pike as you perform the knee twists. Keep your gaze slightly forward to maintain a neutral neck position.

1585.description: Weighted Plank Pike Jumps is a challenging exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs. It combines the stability of a plank with explosive plyometric movements to build full-body strength and power.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and raise your hips up and back, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body.
Explosively jump your feet forward towards your hands, bringing your hips up and forward in a powerful pike motion.
Immediately reverse the movement, jumping your feet back to the starting high plank position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.

1584.description: The Weighted Plank Pikes is a challenging core and upper body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It involves transitioning from a plank position to a pike position while holding a weight, promoting overall body strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core muscles to maintain a neutral spine.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or plate, between your feet or ankles. This added resistance will challenge your core and upper body.
Keeping your legs straight, raise your hips up and back to form an inverted 'V' shape with your body, bringing your feet closer to your hands.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting plank position.

1586.description: The Weighted Plank to Stand Up is a total-body exercise that challenges core strength, stability, and mobility. It involves transitioning from a plank position to a standing position while holding a weight, engaging multiple muscle groups throughout the movement.
instructions: Assume a high plank position on the floor, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles.
Hold a weight (dumbbell or kettlebell) between your feet, keeping your arms extended.
Maintaining a neutral spine, engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your hips up and back, transitioning into a standing position while keeping the weight between your feet.
Reverse the movement by hinging at the hips to lower your body back into the plank position, keeping the weight elevated throughout.

1587.description: The Weighted Plank With Arm Raise is a challenging core and upper body exercise that engages multiple muscle groups while improving stability and balance.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and glutes.
Slowly raise one arm out in front of you, keeping your shoulder, hips, and feet aligned.
Hold the arm raise for a moment, then lower your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat with the opposite arm, maintaining a stable plank position throughout the movement.
Optionally, you can hold a light dumbbell in the raised hand to increase the resistance and challenge.
Perform equal reps on each side, focusing on proper form and controlled movements.

1588.description: The Weighted Plank With Knee to Elbow is a challenging core and stability exercise that engages multiple muscle groups. It requires full-body engagement and improves overall strength and endurance.
instructions: Assume a high plank position on the floor, engaging your core and maintaining a straight line from your head to heels.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell securely against your chest.
Slowly bring your right knee towards your left elbow, then return to the starting position. Repeat on the opposite side.
Maintain a stable plank position throughout the movement, avoiding any rocking or sagging of the hips.
Perform the exercise for the desired number of repetitions or duration, switching sides evenly.

1589.description: The Weighted Plank with Oblique Crunch is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and obliques. It challenges stabilization and strengthens the midsection.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, engaging your core and maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back, keeping your shoulders retracted and your elbows tucked close to your body.
Slowly lower your right elbow to the floor, then your left, lowering into a forearm plank position.
Pause, then drive through your forearms to return to the starting high plank position.
Repeat on the other side, lowering your left elbow first, then your right.
After completing the plank portion, brace your core and perform 5-10 controlled oblique crunches, lifting your hips and twisting to the right, then the left.

1948.description: The Weighted Plie Slides is a lower body strength exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. This exercise improves stability, balance, and muscular endurance.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes turned outward in a plie stance, and hold a weight plate at chest level.
Keeping your chest up and core braced, slowly lower into a plie squat position by bending at the hips and knees, ensuring your knees track over your toes.
Once you reach the bottom of the squat, pause briefly, then drive through your heels to slide back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1949.description: The Weighted Plie Squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and inner thighs. It challenges balance and stability while strengthening the legs.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest, keeping your core engaged.
Initiate the movement by sending your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a deep squat, keeping your chest up and weight in your heels.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position.

1590.description: The Weighted Plyometric Side Plank is a challenging core and stabilization exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It strengthens the obliques, shoulders, and hips while also improving balance and explosive power.
instructions: Begin by lying on your side with your elbow directly under your shoulder and your legs stacked on top of each other.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from your head to your feet. Hold a weight plate, dumbbell, or other weight against your chest.
Explosively jump your feet a few inches off the floor, keeping your body in a straight line. Return your feet to the starting position with control.
Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch and repeat on the opposite side.

1087.description: The Weighted Power Squat Chop is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and core. It helps develop explosive power, strength, and functional movement patterns.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or weight plate at chest height with both hands.
Initiate the movement by driving your hips back and bending your knees to perform a controlled squat, keeping your chest up and core braced.
As you drive back up to the starting position, explosively rotate your torso and extend your arms, swinging the weight diagonally across your body.
Reverse the motion, bringing the weight back to the starting position at chest height, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1317.description: The Weighted Pretzel Side Kick is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and core. It challenges balance and stability while building lower body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight at chest height with both hands.
Shift your weight to your left foot and lift your right leg out to the side, keeping the knee bent and the weight close to your body.
Extend your right leg out to the side, straightening the knee but keeping the leg slightly bent.
Pause briefly, then return your right leg to the starting position by drawing it back in towards your left leg.

1950.description: The Weighted Prisoner Squat is a compound exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core. This exercise helps to improve overall lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight (e.g., dumbbell, kettlebell) at your chest with both hands.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat position, ensuring your knees track over your toes.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the squat, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Maintain proper form throughout the movement, keeping your back straight and your elbows close to your body.

1318.description: The Weighted Prone Hip Internal Rotation is a strength-building exercise that targets the hip rotator muscles, helping to improve overall hip mobility and stability.
instructions: Lie face-down on a flat surface, keeping your legs extended and feet shoulder-width apart.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell between your ankles, ensuring it is centered and secure.
Engage your core and slowly rotate your thighs inward, bringing your knees towards the midline of your body.
Hold the contracted position for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position by rotating your thighs outward.

1682.description: The Weighted Pull Up is a compound exercise that targets the major upper body pulling muscles, including the lats, biceps, and back. It is an excellent way to build upper body strength and muscle mass.
instructions: Secure a weight, such as a dumbbell or weight plate, between your feet or ankles.
Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades together as you initiate the movement by pulling your body up until your chin is above the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the exercise.

1743.description: The Weighted Push Up is a strength training exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It helps build upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, feet hip-width apart, and a weight plate or dumbbell positioned on your upper back.
Engage your core and maintain a straight body alignment from head to heels throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows and keeping them close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the ground, pause briefly, then push yourself back up to the starting position by fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the exercise.

1744.description: The Weighted Push Up And Row is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and back. It combines the push-up motion with a rowing movement to build upper body strength and muscle definition.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your core engaged. Place a dumbbell or other weight under your chest.
Perform a push-up, lowering your chest towards the weight and then pressing back up to the starting position.
At the top of the push-up, row the weight towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Pause briefly, then lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining good form throughout the exercise.

1745.description: The Weighted Push-Up Plus is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It adds a resistance element to the push-up motion to build upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart, your core engaged, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other resistance object on your upper back, just below your neck.
Keeping your core braced, slowly lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, then push back up to the starting position.
As you push back up, finish the movement by squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the push-up, engaging your upper back muscles.

1746.description: The Weighted Push Up With Feet on Swiss Ball is a challenging strength training exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It requires core stabilization and balance.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and place your feet on top of it, keeping your legs extended.
Grip a dumbbell with both hands and assume a push-up position, with your hands directly beneath your shoulders.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Slowly lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, then push back up to the starting position.

1747.description: The Weighted Push Up With One Hand On Medicine Ball is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles, while also engaging the core and stabilizing muscles. This exercise adds an unstable surface to the push-up, requiring increased muscle activation and balance.
instructions: Place a medicine ball on the floor and position your hands shoulder-width apart, with one hand on the medicine ball and the other on the floor.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a straight line from your heels to the top of your head.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor, bending your elbows and keeping them close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the floor, push back up to the starting position by fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch hands and repeat on the other side.

1319.description: The Weighted Quadruped Hip Extension is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back muscles. It involves extending the hip while in a quadruped position, with the addition of a weight for increased resistance.
instructions: Begin in a quadruped position on the floor, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Engage your core and place a weight (such as a dumbbell or kettlebell) between your thighs, just above your knees.
Slowly lift your right leg straight back, keeping your knee bent and the weight secure between your thighs.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower your leg back to the starting position.
Repeat with the left leg, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

1422.description: The Weighted Quadruped Leg Raise is a core and lower body strengthening exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back muscles. It challenges stability and balance while engaging the posterior chain.
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands shoulder-width apart and your knees hip-width apart. Engage your core.
Keeping your leg straight, lift one leg up towards the ceiling, squeezing your glute at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position. Repeat on the same side for the desired number of reps before switching legs.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement and avoid arching your back or swinging your leg.

1320.description: The Weighted Quadruped with Leg Lift is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, back, and hips. It challenges stability and coordination while strengthening the posterior chain.
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands shoulder-width apart and knees hip-width apart. Engage your core to maintain a neutral spine.
Lift one leg straight back, keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle. Simultaneously extend the opposite arm forward, maintaining a straight line from your raised hand to your raised foot.
Slowly lower your leg and arm back to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.
Keep your movements controlled and avoid arching your back. Maintain good posture throughout the exercise.

1184.description: The Weighted Raised Legs Crunch is a targeted abdominal exercise that engages the core muscles to improve strength and stability. This variation adds resistance to challenge the abdominals further.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and a dumbbell held between your feet.
Engage your core and raise your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them straight.
Slowly lower your legs back down until they are a few inches from the floor, then raise them back up.
As you raise your legs, simultaneously contract your abdominal muscles to perform a crunch, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.

1884.description: The Weighted Reclining Circle is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups by challenging stabilization and mobility through circular movements performed in a reclined position.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a light dumbbell or weight plate at chest level.
Slowly lower the weight out to the side, keeping your arms extended, then reverse the movement to bring the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement in a circular pattern, controlling the weight throughout the range of motion.
Maintain a neutral spine and engage your core muscles to stabilize your body during the exercise.

1185.description: The weighted reverse crunch is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It helps to develop core stability and improve overall strength in the midsection.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lift your hips off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring that your lower back remains in contact with the floor throughout the exercise.

1186.description: The Weighted Reverse Crunch on a Bench is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles while also engaging the hip flexors. It is a more advanced variation of the traditional reverse crunch, adding a weight held at the chest for increased resistance and muscle activation.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench or sturdy surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell at your chest, keeping your arms extended.
Engage your core by contracting your abdominal muscles, then slowly lower your torso back towards the bench, keeping your legs straight.
Once your upper back touches the bench, use your abdominal muscles to pull your torso back up to the starting position, lifting your hips off the bench.

1187.description: The Weighted Reverse Curl and Lift is a compound exercise that targets the biceps, forearms, and core muscles. It helps build strength and stability in the upper body while engaging the core for balance and control.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and core engaged.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keeping your elbows close to your sides, curl the weights up towards your shoulders in a controlled motion.
At the top of the movement, rotate your palms to face forward and press the weights overhead, fully extending your arms.
Slowly lower the weights back down, rotating your palms to face up as you return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the movement.

1885.description: The Weighted Reverse Curl Up is a strength-building exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the rectus abdominis and obliques, while also engaging the hip flexors. This exercise helps improve core stability and strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your chest.
Engage your core and slowly curl your upper back off the floor, keeping your lower back in contact with the ground.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your upper back back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1287.description: The Weighted Reverse Hip Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back. It helps improve core stability, hip mobility, and overall lower body strength.
instructions: Lie face-down on the floor with a weight, such as a dumbbell or kettlebell, held between your ankles.
Engage your core and slowly raise your legs and hips off the floor, using your glutes and hamstrings to lift the weight.
Hold the contracted position for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1423.description: The Weighted Reverse Leg Raise targets the posterior chain muscles, including the glutes and hamstrings, while also engaging the core. It improves lower body strength, stability, and hip mobility.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your legs extended and a weight plate or dumbbell held between your ankles.
Engage your core and slowly raise your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.

1424.description: The Weighted Reverse Leg Raise on a Swiss Ball targets various lower body and core muscles, helping to improve strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and sit on it, keeping your feet flat on the floor and your back straight.
Engage your core and slowly lower your torso towards the floor, keeping your legs straight and raising them up towards the ceiling.
At the top of the movement, hold for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back down towards the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.

1481.description: The Weighted Reverse Lunge With Reach Back is a compound lower-body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core and improving balance and stability.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height with your palm facing inward.
Step back with the opposite leg, lowering your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee nearly touches the floor.
As you lunge back, reach the free arm back behind you, maintaining a straight torso and avoiding leaning forward.
Push back to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Repeat on the other side, alternating legs with each repetition.

1482.description: The Weighted Reverse Lunge With Twist And Overhead Reach is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and core, while also improving stability and balance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in both hands at chest height.
Take a large step back with your right leg, lowering your body until your right knee nearly touches the floor.
As you lunge back, rotate your torso to the right and reach the dumbbell overhead with your right arm.
Push back to the starting position, bringing the dumbbell back to chest height.
Repeat the movement on the other side, stepping back with the left leg and twisting to the left.
Continue alternating sides, maintaining proper form and control throughout the movement.

1483.description: The Weighted Reverse Sliding Box Lunge is a lower body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging core stability. This exercise incorporates a sliding motion to challenge balance and coordination.
instructions: Stand facing away from a sturdy box or bench, holding a dumbbell or weight plate at chest level with both hands.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and initiate the movement by sliding your left leg back, bending both knees to lower your body into a reverse lunge position.
Press through your right heel to return to the starting position, keeping your torso upright throughout the movement.
Repeat on the opposite side, sliding your right leg back into a reverse lunge, then pressing back to the starting position.

1484.description: The Weighted Reverse Sliding Lunge is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It helps improve overall lower body strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at your side.
Step back with the opposite leg, lowering your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee almost touches the floor.
Push back to the starting position by driving through your front heel, then repeat on the opposite side.
Maintain an upright torso and keep your core engaged throughout the movement.

1389.description: The Weighted Ring Dip is a compound exercise that primarily targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles, while also engaging the core. It adds an extra challenge by incorporating weight, such as a dumbbell or weight plate, to increase the resistance and intensity of the movement.
instructions: Adjust the height of the rings or parallel bars to allow your arms to fully extend with a slight bend in the elbows.
Grip the rings or bars with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and position your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower your body by bending at the elbows, keeping them close to your sides, until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back up to the starting position by fully extending your arms, squeezing your chest and triceps at the top of the movement.

1748.description: The Weighted Ring Handstand Push-Up is an advanced strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the shoulders, chest, and core. This exercise requires significant upper body and core strength, balance, and control.
instructions: Secure a set of suspension rings at a height that allows you to fully extend your arms in a handstand position.
Load a weight plate or dumbbell on your lower back, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Kick up into a handstand position, maintaining a tight core and controlled movement.
Slowly lower your body until your head nearly touches the floor, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press back up to the starting handstand position, fully extending your arms.

1390.description: The Weighted Ring Muscle Up is a challenging upper body exercise that combines a pull-up and a dip to build strength and power in the back, shoulders, and arms.
instructions: Grasp the rings with an overhand grip and hang at arm's length with your body in a straight line.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulders back and driving your elbows toward your hips, lifting your body until your chin is above the rings.
Forcefully push your body up by straightening your arms and driving your shoulders down until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

1591.description: The Weighted Rolling Side Plank is a compound core exercise that challenges stability and strengthens the obliques, transverse abdominis, and other stabilizing muscles.
instructions: Start in a side plank position with your forearm on the ground and your feet stacked.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate just above your shoulder with your free hand.
Brace your core and slowly roll your body forward and back, keeping your hips stable and body in a straight line.
Perform the desired number of reps on each side, then switch and repeat on the opposite side.

1391.description: The Weighted Rope Climb is a full-body strength exercise that challenges the upper body, core, and leg muscles. It improves grip strength, shoulder stability, and overall muscular endurance.
instructions: Secure a heavy rope or climbing rope to a high anchor point, ensuring it can support your body weight.
Grip the rope firmly with both hands, engaging your core and maintaining a straight body position.
Using your arms and legs, pull yourself up the rope, maintaining control and a steady pace.
Once you reach the top, slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, resting as needed between sets.

1188.description: The Weighted Rotational Lift is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups by combining a squat, overhead press, and rotational movement. It helps improve overall strength, stability, and core engagement.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell in front of your chest with both hands.
Initiate the movement by hinging at the hips and bending your knees to lower into a squat position, keeping your chest up and core engaged.
As you stand back up, press the weight overhead, straightening your arms and engaging your shoulders.
Rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips stationary, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the left, then lower the weight back to the starting position in front of your chest.

1785.description: The Weighted Row is a compound strength exercise that primarily targets the back muscles, including the lats, traps, and rhomboids. This exercise is effective for building upper body strength and muscle mass.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hinge forward at the hips to create a flat back position.
Grip a dumbbell or kettlebell with an overhand grip and let it hang directly below your shoulder.
Initiate the movement by driving your elbow straight back, squeezing your shoulder blade as you pull the weight up towards your chest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

1485.description: The Weighted Runners Lunge to Balance is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups while challenging balance and coordination. It combines a weighted lunge with a balance component, enhancing lower body strength, stability, and overall functional fitness.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Take a large step forward with the opposite leg, lowering your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Pause, then drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, keeping your torso upright and core engaged throughout the movement.
Repeat on the same side for the desired number of reps, then switch legs and perform the same number of reps on the other side.
After completing the lunge reps, hold the final lunge position and lift your back heel off the floor, balancing on your front foot for 2-3 seconds.
Carefully return your back heel to the floor, then step back to the starting position.
Repeat the lunge and balance sequence on the opposite leg.

1886.description: The Weighted Russian Twist on Swiss Ball is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the oblique muscles and improves trunk stability and rotational power.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your back straight and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Engage your core and slowly lower your upper body back until your back is supported by the ball.
Keeping your core braced, twist your torso to the right, then to the left, tapping the weight on the floor on each side.
Repeat the twisting motion in a controlled manner, keeping your hips stationary throughout the movement.

1189.description: The Weighted Seated Alternating Reverse Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. It involves lifting the legs and torso while seated, challenging the abdominal muscles to stabilize the spine.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, holding a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button in towards your spine.
Exhale and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, curling your torso up and bringing your knees towards your chest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating between left and right with each repetition.

1034.description: The Weighted Seated Calf Raise is an effective exercise that targets the calf muscles, primarily the gastrocnemius and soleus. This exercise helps to improve lower body strength and muscle development.
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other weighted object on your thighs, just above your knees.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you slowly raise your heels off the floor, contracting your calf muscles.
Hold the contraction for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your heels back to the starting position.

1190.description: The Weighted Seated Leg U is a strength-building exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the legs, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It helps improve lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you, holding a dumbbell or weight plate between your feet.
Engage your core and lift your legs up, forming a 'U' shape with your body. Avoid arching your back.
Hold the contracted position for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring controlled movement throughout the exercise.

1854.description: The Weighted Serratus Chair Shrug is a targeted exercise that works the serratus anterior muscles, which are responsible for stabilizing and protracted the scapulae. This exercise can help improve shoulder mobility and posture.
instructions: Sit upright in a chair or on a bench, holding a dumbbell or other weight in each hand with your arms extended at your sides.
Keeping your core engaged and shoulders back, slowly shrug your shoulders up towards your ears, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold the shrug position for a brief moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring that your movement is controlled and focused on the serratus anterior muscles.

1855.description: The Weighted Serratus Shrug is a strength-building exercise that primarily targets the serratus anterior muscles, which are responsible for stabilizing the scapula and improving shoulder mobility.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your body.
Keeping your core engaged, raise your shoulders straight up towards your ears, focusing on contracting the serratus anterior muscles.
Hold the top position for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring that you maintain proper form throughout the movement.

1749.description: The Weighted Shoulder Push-Up is a compound exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps, while also engaging the core muscles for stabilization. This variation adds resistance to the traditional push-up, increasing the challenge and muscle activation.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands positioned slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart.
Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back, just below the neck, to provide additional resistance.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your body until your chest nearly touches the ground, maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Exhale as you push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

1118.description: The Weighted Side Abs Leg Lift is a core-focused exercise that targets the obliques and challenges stability. It helps develop functional strength and muscular endurance in the midsection.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and your right arm extended on the floor to support your upper body.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet, keeping your legs straight and together.
Engage your core and lift your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them straight and controlled.
Slowly lower your legs back down, keeping tension in your obliques throughout the movement.
Complete the desired number of reps, then switch sides and repeat on the opposite side.

1486.description: The Weighted Side and Crossover Lunge is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and gluteal muscles. This exercise improves lower body strength, stability, and mobility.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in one hand at shoulder height.
Take a large step out to the side with the opposite leg, keeping your torso upright and your weight distributed evenly.
Bend both knees to lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee nearly touches the ground.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, then repeat the movement on the other side.
For the crossover lunge, take a step forward and across your body with one leg, lowering your body into a lunge before returning to the starting position.
Alternate sides with each repetition, maintaining control and balance throughout the movement.

1119.description: The Weighted Side Bend is a strength training exercise that targets the oblique muscles, improving lateral core stability and strength.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight at your side with an overhand grip.
Keeping your back straight, slowly bend your torso to the side, moving the weight down towards the floor while keeping your hips stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then return to the starting position by contracting the oblique muscles on the opposite side.
Repeat the movement on the other side, alternating between left and right for the desired number of repetitions.

1592.description: The Weighted Side Kick Plank is a full-body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and glutes, while also improving balance and stability.
instructions: Assume a side plank position on your right forearm, with your feet stacked and a dumbbell held at shoulder height in your left hand.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lift your left leg straight up, keeping it parallel to the floor, then slowly lower it back down.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat the exercise on the other side.

1487.description: The weighted side lunge is a strength-training exercise that targets the lower body, particularly the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It also engages the core muscles for stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Keeping your torso upright, step out to the side with the opposite leg, lowering your hips until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push back to the starting position and repeat on the other side, alternating legs with each repetition.
Maintain control throughout the movement and keep your core engaged to ensure proper form.

1488.description: The Weighted Side Lunge Sweep is a strength training exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core. It challenges stability and balance while improving lower body strength and mobility.
