instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Take a large step out to the side with the opposite leg, lowering your hips and bending both knees to perform a side lunge.
As you lunge, sweep the weight across your body, lowering it toward the floor on the opposite side of your front leg.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, bringing the weight back to the starting position.

1489.description: The Weighted Side Lunge to Crossover Tap is a multi-joint exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core. It challenges stability, balance, and coordination while promoting lower-body strength and power.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in one hand at your side.
Take a large step out to the side with the leg on the same side as the weight, keeping your torso upright and core engaged.
Bend your hips and knees to lower your body into a side lunge, keeping your weight-bearing knee in line with your ankle.
Press through your heel to return to the starting position, then tap the weight across your body in front of you, lowering it towards the opposite foot.
Repeat the lunge and crossover tap on the same side for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1321.description: The Weighted Side Lying Leg Raise is a strength exercise that targets the hip abductors and core muscles. It helps to strengthen the hips, improve stability, and enhance overall lower body strength.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and a dumbbell or ankle weight secured just above your ankles.
Engage your core and slowly raise your top leg as high as you comfortably can, keeping it in line with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and complete the same number of reps on the other leg.

1593.description: The weighted side plank is a strength-building exercise that targets the core muscles, particularly the obliques. It challenges stability and engages the entire side of the body.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and your right elbow directly under your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate vertically in your left hand, extending your left arm toward the ceiling.
Hold this position, keeping your body in a straight line, for the desired duration.
Repeat on the opposite side.

1594.description: The Weighted Side Plank and Row is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and back. It improves core stability, shoulder strength, and grip strength.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your right elbow directly under your shoulder and your legs stacked. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand with your arm extended.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, supporting your body on your right elbow and feet.
Keeping your core braced, row the dumbbell up toward your chest, squeezing your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the process on the other side.

1595.description: The Weighted Side Plank Lift is a challenging core exercise that targets the obliques, transverse abdominis, and stabilizing muscles. It helps improve overall core strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and feet stacked. Prop your upper body up on your right elbow and forearm, keeping your shoulder directly over your elbow.

Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Hold a dumbbell or weight plate in your left hand, extending your arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Slowly lower the weight towards the floor, keeping your core braced and your body in a straight line. Pause briefly at the bottom, then press the weight back up to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps, then switch sides and repeat on the left.

1596.description: The Weighted Side Plank With Elbow On Bosu Ball is a challenging core strengthening exercise that targets the obliques, abdominals, and stabilizing muscles of the trunk and hips.
instructions: Set up a Bosu ball on the floor with the rounded side facing up.
Lie on your right side with your right elbow and forearm resting on the center of the Bosu ball, your legs extended and stacked.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, supporting your body weight on your right forearm and the outer edge of your right foot.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate in your left hand, extending your arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Hold this side plank position, focusing on keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels, for the desired duration before switching sides.

1597.description: The Weighted Side Plank with Feet on Bench is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the obliques, core, and stabilizing muscles. This variation adds an external load to increase the challenge and engage the muscles more effectively.
instructions: Set up a bench or stable surface at hip height.
Lie on your side with your feet on the bench and your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Engage your core, lift your hips off the floor, and hold a dumbbell or weight plate with your top hand.
Hold the side plank position, keeping your body in a straight line from your head to your feet, for the desired duration.

1598.description: The Weighted Side Plank with Knee Circle is a challenging core exercise that strengthens the obliques, abdominals, and shoulder stabilizers. It also improves balance and body control.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and feet stacked. Prop your upper body up on your right elbow and forearm, keeping your shoulder directly over your elbow.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Hold a dumbbell or weight plate against your chest with both hands.
Keeping your core braced, slowly circle your left knee forward, out, and back to the starting position. Complete 8-10 controlled circles before switching sides.
Maintain a stable side plank position throughout the movement, ensuring your hips do not sag or hike up. Focus on engaging your obliques to drive the knee circle.

1599.description: The Weighted Side Plank with Knee Tuck is a challenging core and stability exercise that targets the obliques, transverse abdominis, and hip flexors. It helps improve overall core strength and stability.
instructions: Lie on your right side, with your legs straight and your right elbow directly under your shoulder. Place a dumbbell or weight plate on your hip.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Keeping your core tight, bring your left knee towards your chest, then return it to the starting position.
Repeat the knee tuck for the desired number of reps, then switch sides and repeat on the other side.

1600.description: The Weighted Side Plank with Leg Lift is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, obliques, and hip abductors. This exercise challenges stability and engages the entire body while incorporating a leg lift for added difficulty.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and your right elbow directly under your shoulder, palm flat on the floor.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your heels. Hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Keeping your core braced, lift your top leg as high as comfortable while maintaining good form.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise.

1601.description: The Weighted Side Plank with Reach Under is a challenging core-strengthening exercise that targets the obliques, transverse abdominis, and shoulder stabilizers. It improves overall trunk stability and mobility.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs extended and feet stacked. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your right hip and prop yourself up on your right elbow and forearm.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Reach your left arm up toward the ceiling.
Slowly lower your left arm behind your back, reaching under your body, then return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat the movement on the opposite side.

1358.description: The Weighted Side Step is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups in the lower body. It helps improve lateral movement, stability, and balance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and core engaged.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or kettlebell, at chest height with both hands.
Take a large step to the side with one leg, keeping the other leg stationary.
Push through the heel of the stepping leg to return to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.
Maintain good posture throughout the movement, keeping your back straight and chest up.

1191.description: The Weighted Side to Side Crunch and Weave is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the oblique muscles while also engaging the rectus abdominis. This exercise helps improve lateral flexion, rotation, and stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lower your knees to the left, keeping your shoulders and upper back pressed into the floor.
Pause briefly, then return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
As you lower your knees, simultaneously reach the weight diagonally across your body in the opposite direction, creating a 'weaving' motion.
Continue alternating sides, keeping your core engaged and moving with control throughout the movement.

1490.description: The Weighted Side To Side Lunge Chops is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, including the legs, core, and shoulders. It helps to improve overall strength, stability, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands at chest height.

Take a large step to the right, lowering your hips and bending your right knee to perform a side lunge. As you lunge, simultaneously rotate your torso and swing the weight diagonally across your body, from the right shoulder to the left hip.
Push back to the starting position and repeat the movement on the opposite side, stepping to the left and swinging the weight from the left shoulder to the right hip.
Maintain proper form throughout the movement, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.

1648.description: The Weighted Side to Side Shuffle Jump is a plyometric exercise that challenges lateral movement, explosive power, and coordination. It targets various lower body muscle groups and improves overall athletic performance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Initiate the movement by quickly shuffling your feet to the right, then explosively jump up and to the left, bringing your feet together in the air.
Land softly on your left foot, then immediately shuffle your feet back to the right and repeat the explosive jump to the left.
Continue alternating side-to-side shuffle jumps, maintaining control and proper form throughout the set.

1491.description: The Weighted Siff Jump Lunge is a dynamic lower body exercise that challenges balance, coordination, and explosive power. It targets the major muscle groups of the legs, hips, and core.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Initiate the movement by sending your hips back and bending your knees to lower into a lunge position, keeping your chest upright.
Explosively drive through the front heel to jump up, bringing your back leg forward to meet the front leg in a split-stance position.
Land softly with control, immediately lowering back down into the lunge position on the opposite side.

1786.description: The Weighted Single Arm Inverted Row is a compound strength exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the back, biceps, and core. This exercise challenges unilateral stability and engages the muscles of the upper body and torso.
instructions: Set up a sturdy table or bench at hip height. Grip the edge with one hand and extend your legs out in front of you, keeping your body in a straight line.
Keeping your core braced, pull your shoulder blade down and back, rowing your hand toward your chest while maintaining a neutral wrist position.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1750.description: The Weighted Single Arm Medicine Ball Push Up is a challenging upper body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It requires core stability and unilateral strength to perform effectively.
instructions: Hold a medicine ball with one hand and assume a push-up position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the floor, press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arm.

1359.description: The Weighted Single Leg Back Extension is a compound exercise that targets the posterior chain muscles, primarily the lower back and gluteus maximus. It helps to improve core stability, spinal mobility, and overall lower body strength.
instructions: Stand behind a sturdy bench or chair, holding a dumbbell or weight plate at your chest.
Engage your core and shift your weight onto one leg, lifting the other leg behind you.
Keeping your back flat, hinge forward at the hips to lower your torso, maintaining a neutral spine.
Once you feel a stretch in your hamstring, reverse the movement by driving through your heel to return to the starting position.

1999.description: The Weighted Single Leg Bench Dip and Kick is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the triceps, shoulders, and core. It challenges balance and stability while building lower body strength.
instructions: Sit on a sturdy bench or box with your hands gripping the edge, fingers facing forward. Extend your legs out in front of you, keeping one foot planted and the other leg raised.
Straighten your arms to lift your body off the bench, lowering your hips toward the floor while keeping your core engaged.
Pause briefly, then push back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch legs and repeat.
As you perform the dip, simultaneously kick your raised leg out in front of you, then return it to the starting position. Coordinate the leg kick with the bench dip motion.

1951.description: The Weighted Single Leg Bench Get Up is a compound exercise that challenges core stability, balance, and full-body strength. It involves transitioning from a seated position on a bench to a standing position while holding a weight on one side.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with one leg extended and the other foot flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in the hand opposite the extended leg.
Brace your core and drive through your planted foot to stand up, straightening your extended leg as you rise.
Once standing, return to the starting seated position by bending at the hips and knees to lower your body back down to the bench.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side, then switch legs and repeat.

1952.description: The Weighted Single Leg Bench Squat is a compound exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes while also engaging the core for stability. It challenges unilateral lower body strength and balance.
instructions: Stand facing a bench with one foot placed firmly on the bench and the other foot on the floor, holding a dumbbell at your side.
Keep your core engaged and maintain good posture throughout the movement.
Initiate the squat by bending at the hip and knee of your working leg, lowering your body until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Press through your heel to return to the starting position, squeezing your glute at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and perform the same number of reps.

1035.description: The Weighted Single Leg Bent Knee Calf Raise targets the calf muscles, improving lower body strength and balance. It involves lifting your bodyweight on one leg while holding a weight in the opposite hand.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Shift your weight onto one leg, bending the opposite knee slightly and keeping it in line with your hip.
Engaging your calf muscle, slowly raise up onto your toes, lifting your bodyweight.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower back down with control.
Complete the desired number of reps, then switch legs and repeat.

2000.description: The Weighted Single Leg Dip is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It helps to develop single-leg strength, balance, and stability.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Bend at the hip and knee to lower your body, keeping your torso upright and your core engaged.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press back up to the starting position, squeezing the working leg's glute at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch sides.

1036.description: The Weighted Single Leg Donkey Calf Raise is a calf-strengthening exercise that targets the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles. This exercise improves lower leg strength and stability, particularly beneficial for athletes and individuals seeking to enhance their athletic performance or overall leg power.
instructions: Stand with your back facing a sturdy wall or chair, and place one foot firmly on the ground in front of you.
Engage your core and lift your other foot off the ground, balancing solely on the working leg.
Holding a dumbbell or other weight between your shoulder blades, slowly raise your body by lifting your heel off the ground, contracting your calf muscle.
At the top of the movement, pause briefly, then slowly lower your body back down, controlling the descent.

1602.description: The Weighted Single Leg Elevated Feet Plank is a challenging core and full-body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, obliques, and stabilizing muscles. It requires balance, stability, and controlled movement.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your feet elevated on a bench or other sturdy surface, engaging your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lift one leg off the surface, keeping it extended and parallel to the ground. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell on the opposite side of your raised leg.
Maintain a tight core and controlled movement as you hold the plank position, focusing on keeping your hips level and avoiding any rotation or sagging.
Switch sides halfway through the set, keeping the weight on the opposite side of your elevated leg.

1603.description: The Weighted Single Leg Flex and Extend is a challenging strength-building exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It improves balance, stability, and unilateral lower body strength.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a dumbbell or other weight in the opposite hand, with your arm extended at shoulder height.
Keeping your torso upright, bend your standing leg to lower your hips and flex your knee, keeping your weight centered over your foot.
Pause briefly, then drive through your heel to extend your leg, returning to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps, then switch sides and repeat.

1288.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It helps improve hip mobility, stability, and muscular endurance.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg extended. Place a dumbbell or weight plate on the hip of your bent leg.
Engage your core and press your bent-leg heel into the floor to lift your hips up, keeping your body in a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Hold the top position for a moment, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.

1289.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise with Foot on Bench is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It challenges single-leg stability and hip extension.
instructions: Set a bench or platform at hip height and stand next to it, holding a dumbbell or weight plate on one side of your body.
Lift the opposite leg and place the foot on the bench, keeping the hips squared.
Engage your core and gluteal muscles, then drive through your heel to lift your hips up, extending your hip until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1290.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise with Foot on Bosu Ball is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles, while also challenging balance and stability.
instructions: Stand with your back to a sturdy surface and place your right foot on top of a Bosu ball, keeping your left foot flat on the floor.
Engage your core and glutes, then raise your hips off the floor, lifting your body up until your torso and thigh are in a straight line.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.

1291.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise with Foot on Foam Roller is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It challenges single-leg stability and hip extension strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your shoulders, head, and upper back on the floor. Place one foot on a foam roller and extend the other leg straight up toward the ceiling.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate on your hip. Engage your core and glute muscles to lift your hips up, keeping your body in a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.

1292.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise with Foot on Medicine Ball is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It challenges single-leg stability and hip extension while adding resistance to the movement.
instructions: Set up a medicine ball on the floor and stand next to it, with one foot on top of the ball.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate across your hips, keeping your core engaged.
Raise your hips off the floor, extending your hip on the working leg and lifting your body in a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower your hips back down to the starting position in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the same number of reps on the other leg.

1293.description: The Weighted Single Leg Hip Raise With Head On Bosu Ball is a compound exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles, while also improving balance and stability.
instructions: Position a Bosu ball on the floor with the dome side up.
Lie down on the Bosu ball, with your head and upper back resting on the platform and your legs extended in front of you.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate with both hands and place it on your lower abdomen or hips.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the Bosu ball, pressing through your heel and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hips back down, controlling the descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat on the opposite side.
Maintain a stable and controlled movement throughout the exercise, avoiding any swinging or jerking motions.

1425.description: The Weighted Single Leg Lowering Drill is a balance and lower body strength exercise that targets the various muscles of the working leg. This exercise helps to improve unilateral leg strength, stability, and control.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a dumbbell or other weight on the same side.
Keeping the working leg slightly bent, slowly lower your body towards the floor by bending at the hip.
Maintain good posture and control throughout the movement, avoiding excessive forward lean.
Descend until you feel a slight stretch in the hamstring of the working leg, then return to the starting position by driving through the heel to stand back up.

1192.description: The Weighted Single Leg Reverse Crunch is a compound exercise that targets the core muscles, including the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. This exercise helps to improve core strength, stability, and overall functional movement patterns.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and a dumbbell or other weight held between your feet.
Engage your core and lift one leg straight up towards the ceiling, keeping the knee slightly bent.
Slowly lower your leg back down towards the floor, keeping your core engaged, and then repeat with the opposite leg.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your leg, rather than relying on momentum or swinging the leg.

1604.description: The Weighted Single Leg Side Plank is a challenging core exercise that targets the obliques, transverse abdominis, and stabilizing muscles of the hips and shoulders. This variation adds an external load to increase the difficulty and engagement of the core.
instructions: Begin by lying on your right side with your legs straight and feet stacked. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your hips.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, supporting your body weight on your right elbow and forearm. Your body should form a straight line from your shoulders to your feet.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling, keeping your shoulders stacked. Hold this side plank position, engaging your obliques.
After the desired time, lower your hips back down to the floor and repeat on the opposite side.

1953.description: The Weighted Single Leg Squat on Swiss Ball is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and core. It challenges balance and stability while building lower body strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and stand with one foot on the ball, keeping the other foot lifted.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate at chest level with both hands.
Initiate the squat by sending your hips back and bending the standing leg, ensuring your knee tracks over your toes.
Descend until your thigh is parallel to the ground, then drive through your heel to return to the starting position.

1887.description: The Weighted Single Leg Swiss Ball Jackknife is a challenging core and lower body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It improves balance, stability, and overall strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and stand with one foot on the ball, the other foot on the floor slightly in front of you.
Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite the foot on the ball, arm extended straight down.
Keeping your core braced, slowly lower your hips toward the floor by bending at the hips and knee, allowing your free leg to extend behind you.
Once you reach the bottom position, pause briefly, then engage your core to return to the starting position by pressing through your standing heel.

1888.description: The Weighted Sit-Up is a compound exercise that targets the core muscles, including the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. This exercise enhances overall core strength and stability, improving posture and performance in various physical activities.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and keeping your back flat against the floor.
Slowly curl your upper body off the floor, keeping your chin tucked and the weight close to your chest.
At the top of the movement, pause for a moment, then slowly lower your back down to the starting position.

1193.description: The Weighted Skater Crunch Cross is a core-strengthening exercise that targets various muscle groups by combining a skater squat with a weighted crunch cross. It engages the abdominal muscles, obliques, and lower body.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at your chest.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and bend your right knee to perform a skater squat, extending your left leg out to the side.
As you lower down, simultaneously rotate your torso to the left, bringing the weight across your body towards your left hip.
Pause, then return to the starting position by straightening your right leg and bringing the weight back to the center of your chest.
Repeat the movement on the other side, shifting your weight onto your left leg and rotating to the right.

1056.description: Weighted Ski Moguls is a challenging cardio exercise that simulates the motion of skiing through moguls, strengthening various muscle groups while improving cardiovascular endurance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in front of your chest with both hands.
Bend your knees and hips to lower your body, shifting your weight back as if sitting into a chair.
Explosively drive through your heels to stand back up, simultaneously raising the weight overhead.
Immediately lower back down and repeat the squat motion, alternating between lowering and raising the weight.

1322.description: The Weighted Sliding Hip Adduction is a strengthening exercise that targets the muscles involved in hip adduction, which is the movement of the thighs toward the midline of the body. This exercise can help improve hip stability and mobility.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell or other weight between your thighs.
Keeping your upper body stationary, slowly slide your thighs together, squeezing the weight with your inner thighs.
Hold the contracted position for a moment, then slowly slide your thighs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1492.description: The Weighted Sliding Lateral Lunge is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and core. It improves lower-body strength, balance, and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or weight plate at chest level.
Take a large step out to the side with one leg, keeping the other leg stationary.
Bend the stepping leg to lower your body into a lateral lunge, ensuring your knee tracks over your toes.
Push back to the starting position by driving through the heel of the stepping leg.
Repeat on the other side, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

1605.description: The Weighted Spiderman Plank is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, shoulders, and hip flexors. It challenges stability and balance while adding a weighted component to the traditional plank position.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lift one leg and bring your knee toward your elbow on the same side, keeping your hips square and core engaged.
Return your leg to the starting position and repeat with the opposite leg.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate between your feet, maintaining a stable plank position throughout the movement.

1751.description: The Weighted Spiderman Push-Up is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and core, while also improving stability and balance.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and a weight plate or dumbbell positioned between your hands.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your body by bending your elbows and bringing your chest towards the floor.
As you descend, simultaneously lift one leg out to the side, forming a 'spiderman' position with your knee nearly touching the floor.
Push back up to the starting position, returning your leg to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the same side for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1360.description: The Weighted Spine Extension is a strength-building exercise that targets the muscles of the back and core, improving spinal stability and posture.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell behind your head with both hands.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly bend your upper body backward, extending your spine while maintaining a neutral neck position.
Hold the end position for a moment, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending forward, avoiding rounding your back.

1057.description: Weighted Split Jacks is a dynamic plyometric exercise that engages multiple muscle groups and elevates the heart rate for an effective cardiovascular workout.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a light dumbbell or medicine ball at chest height.
Initiate the movement by stepping one leg back into a split stance, simultaneously lowering into a lunge and pressing the weight overhead.
Quickly reverse the motion by jumping your feet together, bringing the weight back to the starting position at chest height.
Alternate the lead leg with each repetition, maintaining control and balance throughout the exercise.

1058.description: The Weighted Squat Jacks is a plyometric exercise that combines a weighted squat with a jumping jack, challenging the lower body, core, and cardiovascular system.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight at chest height with both hands.
Initiate the movement by bending at the hips and knees to perform a controlled squat, keeping the chest upright and core engaged.
Immediately drive through the heels to explosively jump, extending the legs and bringing the feet out wide to perform a jumping jack.
Land softly back in the starting squat position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1650.description: The Weighted Squat Jump Onto Box is a plyometric exercise that targets the major lower body muscle groups. This exercise develops explosive power, muscular strength, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell in front of your chest.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to perform a controlled squat.
Explode upward, driving through your heels to jump as high as possible onto the box or platform in front of you.
Land softly on the box with both feet, maintaining control and stability.
Step or jump back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

1649.description: Weighted Squat Jumps In And Out is a plyometric exercise that engages multiple muscle groups and improves explosive power, coordination, and agility. This exercise involves squatting down, jumping out to the sides, and then jumping back in with added weight for resistance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level.
Initiate the movement by bending at the hips and knees to lower into a deep squat position.
Explosively jump out to the sides, landing with feet wider than shoulder-width.
Immediately jump back to the starting position, bringing feet together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and control throughout the movement.

1971.description: The Weighted Squat Plank Push Up is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, core, and upper body. It combines the squat, plank, and push-up movements to challenge total-body strength and stability.
instructions: Holding a weight plate or dumbbell in front of your chest, stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your core engaged, push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat position.
From the bottom of the squat, extend your arms to perform a push-up, maintaining a straight line from your heels to the top of your head.
Push back up to the starting squat position, then stand up tall, lifting the weight to chest height.

1972.description: The Weighted Squat Thrust is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups, primarily targeting the lower body and core. It combines a squat motion with an explosive push-up movement, building overall strength and power.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or weight plate at chest height.
Initiate the movement by bending at the hips and knees to lower into a squat position, keeping the chest upright.
Explosively drive through the heels to extend the hips and knees, propelling the body into a plank position with the weight held at chest height.
Immediately reverse the motion by bending at the hips and knees to return to the starting squat position.

1752.description: The Weighted Stacked Feet Push Up is a challenging upper body and core strength exercise that engages multiple muscle groups. By elevating the feet and adding weight, the exercise increases the resistance and difficulty, leading to greater muscle activation and strengthening.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your feet stacked on top of each other, with a weight plate or dumbbell placed on top of your feet.
Engage your core muscles and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your body until your chest nearly touches the ground, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

1753.description: The Weighted Staggered Hands Push-Up is a challenging variation of the classic push-up that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It requires increased stabilization and core engagement due to the uneven hand positioning.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Place a dumbbell or other weighted object under one hand, creating an uneven base.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Slowly lower your chest towards the floor by bending at the elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the floor, pause briefly, then push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the hand positions and perform the same number of reps on the other side.

1954.description: The Weighted Staggered Squat is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It also challenges core stability and balance.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest height.
Take a step back with one leg, keeping your torso upright and your weight evenly distributed.
Bend your knees and hips to lower your body into a staggered squat position, ensuring your front knee is at 90 degrees and your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Press through your front heel to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top.

1323.description: The Weighted Standing Adduction is a strength-building exercise that targets the inner thigh muscles. It involves standing with feet shoulder-width apart and lifting a weighted object towards the midline of the body, engaging the adductor muscles.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weighted object (e.g., dumbbell, kettlebell) at your side with palms facing inward.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly lift the weighted object towards the midline of your body, squeezing your inner thigh muscles as you move the weight.
Hold the contraction for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.

1037.description: The Weighted Standing Calf Raise targets the calf muscles, improving strength, power, and muscle definition in the lower legs. This exercise can be performed with a dumbbell or barbell to add resistance and increase the challenge.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or barbell across the front of your thighs.
Keeping your knees slightly bent, raise up onto your toes, contracting your calf muscles to lift your heels as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down until your heels nearly touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and keeping your core engaged throughout the exercise.

1324.description: The Weighted Standing Hip Abduction is a strength-building exercise that targets the muscles responsible for hip abduction, including the gluteus medius and tensor fasciae latae. This exercise helps improve hip stability, balance, and lower body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or other weight in one hand at your side.
Engage your core and maintain good posture throughout the movement.
Slowly lift the weighted leg out to the side, keeping the knee straight and the foot flexed.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the leg back to the starting position.

1325.description: The Weighted Standing Rear Leg Raise is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles, while also improving balance and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Engage your core and slowly raise the opposite leg straight behind you, keeping the knee slightly bent.
Squeeze your glute at the top of the movement and hold for a moment.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1973.description: The Weighted Standing T Rotation Balance is a full-body exercise that challenges core stability, balance, and shoulder mobility. It targets multiple muscle groups while improving proprioception and kinesthetic awareness.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at chest height with both hands.
Maintaining a tall, neutral spine, slowly extend your arms out to the sides to form a 'T' shape with your body.
Keeping your core engaged, rotate your torso to the right, reaching the weight back behind you while keeping your arms extended.
Reverse the motion, rotating back to the center and then to the left side, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1361.description: The Weighted Static Back Extension is a strength-building exercise that targets the muscles of the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It helps improve spinal stability, posture, and overall core strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a weight plate or dumbbell close to your chest.
Hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged, until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for the desired duration, focusing on squeezing your glutes and engaging your lower back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position by driving through your heels and engaging your glutes.

1194.description: The Weighted Step Climb is a full-body strength exercise that targets various muscle groups by incorporating a stepping motion with added resistance from a weight held in one or both hands.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy step or bench with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Engage your core and step up onto the platform with one foot, followed by the other, straightening your legs to stand fully on the step.
Slowly step back down, leading with the same foot that stepped up first, and repeat the movement on the opposite side.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and gaze forward throughout the exercise to maintain proper form and balance.
Alternate stepping up with your right and left feet for the desired number of repetitions or duration.

1955.description: The weighted step-up is a lower-body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It helps improve lower-body strength, power, and stability.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or step with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with your palms facing inward.
Step up onto the box with one foot, pressing through your heel to lift your body up.
Bring your other foot up to meet the first, contracting your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly step back down, leading with the same foot that stepped up first.

1606.description: The Weighted Straight Arm Plank is a challenging core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, shoulder stabilizers, and upper body strength. By adding weight to the body, it increases the resistance and intensity of the exercise.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms extended, and core engaged.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other weighted object on your upper back, just below your shoulders.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, keeping your body in a rigid, neutral position.
Hold this plank position for the desired duration, focusing on maintaining proper form and engagement throughout your core.

1607.description: The Weighted Straight Arm Plank With Shoulder Touch is a challenging core and shoulder stability exercise that targets the entire core musculature while also engaging the deltoids and triceps. This exercise requires controlled movement and balance to maintain proper form.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your right hand to tap your left shoulder, then return your hand to the starting position.
Repeat the same movement on the opposite side, tapping your right shoulder with your left hand.
Continue alternating between left and right shoulder taps, keeping your core engaged and your body in a straight line.

1956.description: The Weighted Sumo Squat Slide In is a compound exercise that targets various lower body muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core. This exercise helps to improve overall lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, holding a dumbbell or weight plate in front of your chest with both hands.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower your body into a deep sumo squat position, keeping your chest upright and core engaged.
From the bottom of the squat, slide your feet inward, bringing them closer together until they are hip-width apart, maintaining the low squat position.
Reverse the movement by sliding your feet back out to the starting wide sumo stance, then drive through your heels to return to the standing position.

1957.description: The Weighted Sumo Squat to Stand is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings, while also engaging the core. This movement improves lower body strength, flexibility, and overall stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly outward, and hold a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest.
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back while keeping your chest upright and lowering your body into a deep sumo squat position.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then engage your glutes and hamstrings to drive through your heels and stand back up to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the movement.

1958.description: The Weighted Sumo Squat With Rotation is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, glutes, and core. It challenges stability and mobility, while also incorporating a rotational movement to engage the obliques.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell in front of your chest with both hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a deep sumo squat position.
As you descend, rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips stationary.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, then repeat the squat and rotation to the left side.

1362.description: The Weighted Superman From Floor is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves lifting the arms and legs off the ground while holding a weight, engaging the posterior chain muscles.
instructions: Lie face-down on the floor with your arms extended in front of you and your legs straight behind you.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell between your hands, keeping your arms straight.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor, squeezing your glutes and engaging your core.
Hold the contracted position for a moment, then slowly lower back to the starting position.

1326.description: The weighted supine hip internal rotation exercise targets the hip rotator muscles to improve range of motion and stability. This exercise can help enhance overall lower body mobility and strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Place a dumbbell, kettlebell, or other weight between your knees.
Slowly lower your knees to one side, keeping your feet together and the weight between your knees.
Hold the stretched position for a moment, then return your knees to the starting position.

2001.description: The Weighted Suspended Dip is a compound exercise that targets multiple upper body muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It challenges stability and engages the core while also increasing overall upper body strength.
instructions: Set up a pair of suspension straps or TRX at shoulder height.
Grasp the handles and position your body in a straight plank, with your arms extended and hands shoulder-width apart.
Initiate the movement by bending at the elbows to lower your body towards the floor, keeping your core engaged and body in a straight line throughout the descent.
Once your upper arms are parallel to the floor, press back up to the starting position by extending the elbows and squeezing the chest.

1787.description: The Weighted Suspended Inverted Row is a compound exercise that targets the back, biceps, and core muscles, while also improving overall upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Attach a weight or dumbbell to a suspension trainer or a sturdy bar set at about waist height.
Grab the handles or bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and hang from your arms with your body in a straight line from heels to head.
Initiate the movement by driving your elbows back, pulling your shoulder blades together, and lifting your body up until your chest nearly touches the handles or bar.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.

1754.description: The Weighted Suspended Push-Up is a challenging variation of the classic push-up that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. This exercise requires the use of a suspension trainer or TRX system to engage additional stabilizing muscles and increase the overall difficulty.
instructions: Set up a suspension trainer or TRX system at about chest height.
Grasp the handles of the suspension trainer and assume a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core and lower body to maintain a straight, stable body position throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your chest towards the ground, bending at the elbows and keeping them close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the ground, pause briefly, then push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.

1363.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Back Extension targets the lower back and core muscles, helping to improve spinal stability, posture, and overall back strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and lie face down on it, with your hips and upper thighs supported by the ball.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, engage your core, and slowly raise your upper body up, keeping your spine neutral.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.

1195.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Crunch is a core strengthening exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. It combines the instability of a Swiss ball with the added resistance of a weight held behind the head to challenge the core musculature.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and your back straight.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell behind your head, keeping your elbows wide.
Engage your core and slowly curl your upper body forward, bringing your shoulder blades toward your hips.
At the top of the movement, pause briefly, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1364.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Hyperextension is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups, including the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves extending the torso over a Swiss ball while holding a weight, challenging core stability and muscular endurance.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and stand with your hips and thighs resting on the ball, keeping your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a weight (e.g., dumbbell, kettlebell) at chest level, engaging your core muscles.
Slowly lower your torso toward the floor, keeping your back straight and maintaining control of the movement.
Once you feel a stretch in your lower back, pause briefly and then engage your back and glute muscles to lift your torso back to the starting position.

1838.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball I Raise is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles and improves stability. This exercise requires the use of a Swiss ball and added weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, to challenge the core and develop overall strength.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and a weight held at your chest.
Engage your core muscles and slowly recline back, keeping your back straight and your head in line with your spine.
Once you reach a 45-degree angle, pause briefly, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core tight throughout the exercise.

1120.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Jackknife is a comprehensive core strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It engages the abdominal, hip, and back muscles to improve overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Place a Swiss ball behind your hips and extend your legs on the ball, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lower your torso towards the floor, maintaining a tight plank position.
Once your chest nearly touches the floor, pause briefly, then use your abdominal muscles to pull your body back up to the starting position.
Keep your arms extended in front of you throughout the movement to challenge your stability.

1365.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Opposite Arm and Leg Lift is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, back, and hip stabilizers. It challenges balance and coordination while improving overall body stability.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and your core engaged.
Extend your right arm and left leg simultaneously, keeping them parallel to the ground.
Hold this position for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side, extending your left arm and right leg.
Alternate sides, maintaining control and balance throughout the exercise.

1121.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Pike is a challenging core exercise that works the abdominal muscles, shoulders, and upper back. It helps to improve strength, stability, and body control.
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands on a Swiss ball and your feet on the floor, your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and slowly raise your hips up, moving the Swiss ball towards your chest using your arms.
Hold the top position briefly, then slowly lower your body back to the starting plank position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the movement.

1608.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Plank is a compound exercise that strengthens multiple muscle groups in the core, shoulders, and back. It challenges stability and engages the entire body while adding an extra challenge with the weight of a Swiss ball.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and place your feet on top of it, engaging your core.
Extend your arms to the floor and assume a high plank position, maintaining a straight line from your heels to the top of your head.
Holding a dumbbell or weight plate, place it on your lower back, keeping your core braced to support the added resistance.
Hold this plank position, focusing on maintaining proper form and engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.

1609.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Plank Leg Lift is a challenging core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, obliques, and stabilizing muscles. This exercise requires balance and control, promoting overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball behind you and kneel in front of it, facing away from the ball.
Carefully lower your forearms onto the Swiss ball, engaging your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate between your feet, keeping your legs extended.
Slowly raise one leg at a time, lifting the weight off the floor while maintaining the plank position.
Alternate lifting each leg, focusing on keeping your core braced and your body in a straight line throughout the movement.

1610.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Plank With Feet On Bench is a challenging core exercise that works the entire body, improving overall strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Position a sturdy bench or platform about 2-3 feet in front of you.
Place a Swiss ball behind you and kneel down, placing your forearms and elbows on the ball.
Extend your legs, resting your feet on the bench, and engage your core to lift your body into a plank position.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell on your back, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Maintain this position, focusing on keeping your core braced and your glutes and legs engaged.
Hold the plank for the desired duration, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the specified number of sets and reps.

1611.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Prone Jackknife is a challenging core and upper body strength exercise that engages multiple muscle groups and improves overall stability and control.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball on the floor and lie face down with your shins resting on top of the ball, feet shoulder-width apart.
Holding a dumbbell or weight plate in front of your chest, engage your core and slowly raise your hips and legs up, bringing your body into a straight line from heels to head.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your body back down until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and tension throughout the movement.

1755.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Push Up is a challenging exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps, while also engaging the core for stability.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball on the floor and place your hands on the ball, shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and extend your legs, balancing your body weight on your hands and toes.
Slowly lower your chest towards the ball, maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Once your chest nearly touches the ball, push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core braced throughout the exercise.

1756.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Push Up Plus is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It also engages the core muscles for stability and balance.
instructions: Kneel behind a Swiss ball and place your hands on the ball, shoulder-width apart.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back, engaging your core to maintain a neutral spine.
Extend your legs, balancing on your toes, and lower your chest towards the ball, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest and pushing the ball forward with your hands.

1196.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Reverse Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. It involves using a Swiss ball to perform a reverse crunch motion, adding resistance for increased muscle activation.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball and walk your feet forward to roll your back down until your shoulder blades are resting on the ball.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, securely between your thighs or feet.
Engage your core and slowly curl your hips and knees towards your chest, lifting your glutes and lower back off the ball.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1122.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Rollout is a core strengthening exercise that challenges the abdominal and stabilizing muscles while also engaging the shoulder and back muscles. This exercise improves overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball in front of you and kneel behind it, grasping a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Keeping your core braced, slowly roll the ball forward by extending your arms, allowing your body to form a straight line from your head to your knees.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then reverse the motion by pulling the ball back towards your body, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring to keep your body in a straight line throughout the exercise.

1197.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Russian Twist is a core strengthening exercise that targets the oblique muscles. It involves twisting the torso side-to-side while maintaining control of a weighted object on an unstable Swiss ball surface.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball and hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands at chest level.
Engage your core and lean back slightly to create tension in your abdominal muscles.
Slowly twist your torso to the right, tapping the weight to the outside of your right thigh, then twist to the left, tapping the weight to the outside of your left thigh.
Keep your upper body stationary and focus on initiating the movement from your core.
Maintain control throughout the range of motion and avoid excessive rocking or swinging of the ball.

1198.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Side Crunch is a core strengthening exercise that targets the oblique muscles. This exercise helps improve lateral flexion, rotation, and stability of the torso.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with your left side facing the ball. Hold a dumbbell or medicine ball just above your left hip.
Keeping your core engaged, slowly lower your torso to the side, feeling a contraction in your left oblique.
Hold the bottom position for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch and repeat on the other side.

1612.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Side Plank is a compound exercise that engages multiple muscle groups to improve core stability, balance, and overall body strength.
instructions: Lie on your side with your feet stacked and elbow positioned directly under your shoulder on a Swiss ball.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your feet.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest or extend your arm to hold the weight overhead.
Hold this side plank position for the desired duration, then repeat on the opposite side.

1839.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball T Raise is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the shoulders, upper back, and core. It helps improve overall upper body strength, stability, and posture.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball with a dumbbell held at chest level, core engaged.
Keeping your back straight, slowly extend your arms out to the sides until they are in line with your shoulders, forming a 'T' shape.
Pause briefly, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.

1840.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball W Raise is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and back. It helps to improve overall strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball and hold a dumbbell or other weight against your chest with both hands.
Engage your core and slowly raise the weight overhead, extending your arms fully above your head.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and balance throughout the exercise.

1959.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Wall Squat is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body while engaging the core for stability. This exercise enhances overall leg and core strength.
instructions: Position a Swiss ball against a wall and stand with your back against the ball, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell at chest level, engaging your core.
Initiate the squat by sending your hips back, bending your knees, and lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.

1841.description: The Weighted Swiss Ball Y Raise is a strength-building exercise that targets the upper back and shoulder muscles. It helps improve posture, shoulder stability, and overall upper body strength.
instructions: Sit on a Swiss ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing in.
Engage your core and slowly raise your arms out to the sides and up, forming a 'Y' shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining good posture and control throughout the exercise.

1758.description: The Weighted T Push Up is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It helps build upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell between your hands.
Keeping your core engaged, lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows and maintaining a straight body line.
As you lower down, spread your elbows out to the sides, creating a T-shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then push back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles at the top.

1617.description: The Weighted T Stabilization exercise is a core-strengthening movement that challenges the body's stabilizing muscles while incorporating a weighted object. This exercise helps improve overall core stability, balance, and postural control.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight, such as a dumbbell or kettlebell, in one hand at chest level.
Extend the opposite arm and leg, creating a 'T' shape with your body. Maintain a neutral spine and engage your core muscles.
Hold the extended position for a predetermined time, focusing on maintaining stability and balance throughout the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.

2002.description: The Weighted Tabletop Dip is a bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It helps to build upper body strength and improve muscular endurance.
instructions: Sit on a sturdy table or bench with your hands gripping the edge, fingers facing forward.
Extend your legs out in front of you and engage your core to stabilize your body.
Straighten your arms to lift your body off the surface, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Slowly lower your body until your elbows form 90-degree angles, then press back up to the starting position.

1199.description: The Weighted Thoracic Crunches on Foam Roller is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the muscles of the upper back and torso. It helps improve spinal mobility and stability.
instructions: Lie on a foam roller positioned horizontally across your upper back, with your head, shoulders, and upper back resting on the roller and your knees bent.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or medicine ball, at your chest with both hands.
Engage your core muscles and slowly crunch up, lifting your shoulder blades off the roller while keeping your lower back pressed into the roller.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower back down to the starting position.

1889.description: The Weighted Three Part Roll Down is a full-body strength exercise that targets the core, shoulders, and posterior chain. It challenges stability and control while improving mobility and flexibility.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest with both hands.
Keeping your back flat, hinge at the hips to slowly lower your torso, letting the weight guide your descent as you roll down vertebrae by vertebrae.
Once your hands reach the floor, pause briefly, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position, rolling up one vertebrae at a time.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and tension throughout the movement.

1613.description: The Weighted Three Way Plank is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and upper body. This exercise challenges stability and engages the body in multiple planes of motion.
instructions: Assume a high plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels. Place a weight plate or dumbbell on your upper back.

Maintaining a straight body, simultaneously move your right arm and left leg out to the side, then return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side, moving your left arm and right leg out to the side.
Next, simultaneously move your right arm forward and your left leg back, then return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side, moving your left arm forward and right leg back.
Finally, simultaneously move your right arm up and your left leg up, then return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side, moving your left arm up and right leg up.

1788.description: The Weighted Towel Grip Inverted Row is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups by having the user row their bodyweight while gripping a weighted towel. This exercise improves upper body strength, core stability, and grip strength.
instructions: Secure a sturdy table or bench at about hip height. Drape a towel over the edge and hold each end with an overhand grip.
Position your body under the table, legs extended and core braced. Your hands should be directly underneath your chest.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades together, drawing your chest up toward the table in a controlled row motion.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your body back to the starting position with arms extended.

1614.description: The Weighted Towel Plank And Knee In is a full-body strength exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It challenges core stability, upper body strength, and lower body control.
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands on the floor, directly under your shoulders, and a towel or small weight placed on your upper back.
Engage your core, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bring one knee toward your chest, maintaining a tight core and avoiding any sagging or arching in your back.
Return the leg to the starting position and repeat with the opposite leg, alternating sides with controlled movements.

1683.description: The Weighted Towel Pull Up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the major upper body muscle groups, including the back, biceps, and shoulders. It requires the use of a towel or other similar object to increase the difficulty of the traditional pull-up movement.
instructions: Secure one end of a towel over a pull-up bar or other sturdy overhead fixture.
Grab the other end of the towel with both hands, using an overhand grip, and hang from the towel with your arms extended.
Engage your core and pull yourself up by bending your elbows and drawing your shoulder blades together, lifting your chin above the towel.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your upper body throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on proper form and control.

1123.description: The Weighted Triangle Hip Press is a strength-building exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core muscles. It involves pressing the hips upward from a triangular stance to develop lower-body power and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent, holding a dumbbell or weight plate between your thighs.
Keeping your back straight, lower your hips back and down, bending at the hips and knees to form a triangular shape with your body.
Engage your core and glutes, then press your hips upward, straightening your legs to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring your movements are controlled and your form remains consistent throughout the set.

1757.description: The Weighted Triple Stop Push-Up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It involves performing a push-up with three distinct pauses, adding an extra level of difficulty and engagement.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, your core engaged, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Inhale and lower your body until your chest is nearly touching the ground, pausing briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Exhale and push yourself back up, pausing briefly at the top of the movement.
Pause again briefly at the midpoint of the push-up, then continue to the starting position.
Repeat the sequence for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the exercise.

1059.description: The Weighted Triple Under is a challenging cardiovascular exercise that combines the basic jump rope movement with a weighted rope. This exercise engages multiple muscle groups and significantly increases heart rate for an effective full-body workout.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the weighted jump rope in both hands in front of your body.
Initiate the movement by swinging the rope backward behind your body, then bring it forward and up, allowing it to pass under your feet three times in a single jump.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, keeping your knees slightly bent and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Repeat the triple under motion, aiming for a smooth, controlled rhythm and maintaining proper form to prevent injury.

1124.description: The Weighted TRX Suspended Jackknife is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and hip flexors. This exercise challenges stability and engages the entire body for an effective total-body workout.
instructions: Secure the TRX straps at a height that allows your body to form a straight line when in the top position of the exercise.
Grasp the TRX handles and extend your arms, supporting your body in a high plank position with your feet in the TRX foot cradles.
Engage your core and slowly bend at the hips, bringing your knees towards your chest while maintaining a straight body position.
Once your knees are close to your chest, pause briefly, then slowly straighten your legs back to the starting position.

1615.description: The Weighted Turkish Get Up To Side Plank is a compound exercise that challenges full-body strength, stability, and mobility. It targets multiple muscle groups while also improving coordination and core engagement.
instructions: Lie on your side with a dumbbell extended overhead. Brace your core and slowly press the dumbbell straight up, keeping your arm locked out.
