Maintaining a rigid torso, press your feet into the floor and push your hips up into a side plank position. Your top leg should be stacked directly over your bottom leg.
Pause briefly in the side plank, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position, maintaining control of the weight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

1616.description: The Weighted Two Point Plank is a challenging core exercise that engages multiple muscle groups and improves overall body stability and strength.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lift one arm and the opposite leg, extending them out away from your body while maintaining the plank position.
Hold this side plank position for the desired duration, ensuring your hips remain square and your core is engaged.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating between left and right for the prescribed number of repetitions.

1125.description: The Weighted U Boat is a core strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups throughout the body. This exercise challenges core stability and enhances overall body strength.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead and your legs straight. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Engage your core and simultaneously raise your arms, shoulders, and legs off the floor, forming a 'U' shape with your body.
Hold the 'U' position for a moment, focusing on maintaining a tight core and controlled movement.
Slowly lower your arms, shoulders, and legs back to the starting position, keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.

1960.description: The Weighted Uneven Squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also challenging core stability and balance.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Keeping your core engaged, send your hips back and bend your knees to lower your body into a squat position, maintaining an upright torso.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position, ensuring that your weight is evenly distributed across both feet.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the weight to the opposite hand and perform the same number of reps.

1890.description: The Weighted V Up is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, hip flexors, and lower back. It challenges core stability and improves overall body control.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms extended overhead, holding a weight plate or dumbbell securely against your chest.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and slowly raise your legs and torso off the ground, forming a 'V' shape with your body.
Hold the V position for a moment, focusing on keeping your core engaged and maintaining a neutral spine.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position in a controlled motion, being careful not to let your lower back arch.

1493.description: The Weighted Walking Lunge is a lower-body strength exercise that challenges the major muscle groups of the legs while also engaging core stability. This exercise improves muscular endurance, balance, and overall lower-body strength.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing inwards.
Step forward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at 90 degrees.
Push back to the starting position with the front leg and repeat with the opposite leg.
Continue alternating legs, taking a controlled step forward with each repetition.

1392.description: The Weighted Wall Slide is a strength-building exercise that targets various muscle groups by challenging shoulder mobility and core stabilization. It helps improve posture and upper body strength.
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet about 6 inches away and shoulder-width apart.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest with both hands, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Slide your back down the wall, bending your knees and hips to lower your body into a squat position, keeping the weight held at chest level.
Pause, then drive through your heels to slide your body back up the wall to the starting position.

1961.description: The Weighted Wall Squat is a strength-building exercise that targets the major muscle groups of the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core musculature for stability.
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart and slightly in front of you.
Hold a dumbbell or weight plate in front of your chest, arms extended.
Initiate the movement by bending at the hips and knees to lower your body, keeping your back flat against the wall.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground, ensuring your knees stay behind your toes.
Pause briefly, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position.

1684.description: The Weighted Wide Grip Pull Up is a compound exercise that targets the major back muscles, biceps, and forearms. This exercise helps to build overall upper body strength and muscle mass.
instructions: Attach a weight plate or dumbbell between your feet using a dip belt or by holding it securely with your legs.
Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand, wide grip, your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades together, initiating the movement from your back.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, fully contracting your back muscles.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, avoiding swinging or kipping.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the set.

1759.description: The Weighted Wide Hands Push-Up is a variation of the classic push-up that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps while also engaging the core musculature. This exercise challenges stability and strengthens the upper body.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart. Place a weight plate or dumbbell between your hands.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor by bending at the elbows, keeping them tucked close to your body.
Once your chest nearly touches the weight, press back up to the starting position by fully extending your arms.

1618.description: The Weighted Wide Stance Plank With Diagonal Arm Lift is a challenging core and shoulder exercise that engages multiple muscle groups. It helps to improve overall body stability, balance, and strength.
instructions: Assume a plank position on the floor, with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet positioned in a wide stance, about twice shoulder-width.
Engage your core muscles and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.
Hold a weight, such as a dumbbell or kettlebell, in one hand with your arm extended towards the floor.
Slowly raise the weight diagonally up and out, lifting your arm up and away from your body, maintaining a straight arm position.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the opposite arm.
Keep your hips level and avoid sagging or arching your back during the exercise.

1619.description: The Weighted Wide Stance Plank With Diagonal Leg Lift is a challenging core and lower body exercise that targets multiple muscle groups. It improves overall body strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Assume a wide-stance plank position, placing your hands directly under your shoulders. Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Place a weight plate, dumbbell, or other weight on the middle of your back. Ensure the weight is secure and does not interfere with your form.
Lift one leg out to the side, keeping it straight and parallel to the ground. Hold for a moment, then lower it back to the starting position.
Repeat the leg lift on the opposite side, maintaining a stable plank position throughout the movement.

1126.description: The Weighted Windmill Switches is a compound exercise that engages various muscle groups, including the core, shoulders, and legs, to improve overall strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands at chest height.
Keeping your core engaged, hinge at the hips to lower the weight toward the outside of your right foot, maintaining a straight back and tall posture.
Pause briefly, then engage your core to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the left side, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

1891.description: The Weighted X Abs exercise targets the core muscles by combining a lateral plank hold with a crunch motion, creating a challenging full-body workout.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your feet shoulder-width apart, engaging your core and glutes.
Extend your right arm and left leg, creating an 'X' shape with your body.
Slowly lower your right elbow and left knee, bringing them together under your torso in a controlled crunch motion.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side, alternating between left arm and right leg.

1022.description: The wide grip barbell bench press is a compound exercise that primarily targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps muscles. It is an effective strength-building exercise that can help increase upper body pushing power and muscle mass.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes positioned under the barbell. Grip the barbell with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your upper chest, keeping your elbows flared out to the sides at an approximately 45-degree angle from your body.
Pause briefly, then press the bar back up by extending your arms until they are straight, driving through your heels and contracting your chest muscles.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled motion, being careful not to let it touch your chest.

1247.description: The wide grip barbell deadlift is a compound exercise that targets the major muscle groups in the back, hips, and legs, and is an effective exercise for developing overall full-body strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell on the floor in front of you. Bend at the hips and knees to grip the barbell with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back flat, chest up, and core engaged throughout the movement. Initiate the lift by driving through your heels, straightening your hips and knees to stand up with the barbell.
At the top of the lift, squeeze your glutes and hold the position briefly before slowly lowering the barbell back to the floor by bending at the hips and knees.
Maintain control throughout the movement and avoid rounding your back. Focus on keeping the barbell close to your body as you lift and lower it.

1856.description: The wide grip barbell shrug is a strength-building exercise that targets the upper trapezius muscles, helping to develop stronger shoulders and improve overall upper body strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand, wide grip, hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keeping your core engaged and back straight, lift the barbell up towards your chin by shrugging your shoulders straight up towards your ears.
Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a brief pause, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and avoiding excessive momentum.

1235.description: The Wide Grip EZ Bar Biceps Curl is a compound exercise that primarily targets the biceps brachii muscles, promoting muscular development and strength in the upper arms.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an underhand, wide grip.
Initiate the movement by flexing at the elbows and curling the weight up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the movement, pause briefly and contract the biceps, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the exercise, avoiding swinging or using momentum to lift the weight.

1857.description: The Wide Grip Jump Shrug is a full-body strength exercise that targets the trapezius, deltoids, and leg muscles. It combines a vertical jump with a shrug movement to engage multiple muscle groups simultaneously.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell or dumbbell with a wide, overhand grip.
Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Initiate the movement by bending your knees and hinging at the hips to lower your body into a quarter squat position.
Explosively drive through your heels, extending your hips and knees to perform a vertical jump, simultaneously shrugging your shoulders towards your ears.
At the top of the jump, pause briefly and focus on maximizing the shrug movement.
Controlled lower your body back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Keep your elbows high and close to your body throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.

956.description: The wide grip lat pulldown is a compound exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi muscles in the back, while also engaging the biceps. It helps to build upper body strength and improve pull-up/row performance.
instructions: Sit down on the lat pulldown machine and adjust the leg pad so your thighs are securely under it.
Grasp the straight bar with an overhand, wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your core engaged, pull the bar straight down towards your upper chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Pause briefly, then slowly allow the bar to return to the starting position with control.

1494.description: The Wide Grip Overhead Barbell Split Squat is a compound exercise that challenges lower body strength and stability while also engaging the core muscles. It's an effective exercise for improving overall leg and hip strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a wide, overhand grip overhead.
Take a large step forward with one leg, keeping your torso upright and your core engaged.
Slowly lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee almost touches the floor.
Press through your front heel to return to the starting position, then repeat with the opposite leg.

1685.description: The wide grip pull-up is a compound exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi, biceps, and rear deltoids, while also engaging the core muscles. This exercise is effective for building upper body strength and improving pulling power.
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand, wide grip, your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades together, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and back, and use your lats to pull your chin up and over the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.

1789.description: The wide grip seated cable row is a compound strength exercise that primarily targets the muscles of the back, including the latissimus dorsi, trapezius, and rhomboids. This exercise helps to improve upper body pulling strength and muscle development.
instructions: Sit at a cable row station and grasp the wide grip handle with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your core braced, pull the handle towards your upper abdomen by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining good posture throughout the exercise.

1760.description: The wide hands push-up is a variation of the classic push-up that targets a broader range of upper body muscles, including the chest, shoulders, and triceps. This exercise helps to build overall upper body strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands positioned slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core muscles and lower your chest towards the floor by bending at the elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle from your body.
Press back up to the starting position by fully extending your arms, being sure to keep your body in a straight line throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and breathing steadily throughout the exercise.

990.description: The wide stance goblet squat is a compound exercise that primarily targets the shoulders and quadriceps while also engaging the traps, glutes, and biceps. This exercise improves overall lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold a dumbbell vertically at chest height, gripping it at the top with both hands.
Initiate the movement by sending your hips back and bending at the knees to lower your body into a deep squat position, keeping your chest upright and core braced.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

1620.description: The Wide Stance Plank With Diagonal Arm Lift is a strength-building exercise that engages multiple muscle groups across the core, shoulders, and back. It challenges stability and coordination while improving overall body strength.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a neutral spine alignment.
Slowly lift one arm straight out to the side, raising it to shoulder height while keeping your hips and torso stable.
Lower the arm back to the starting position and repeat with the opposite arm in a controlled, diagonal motion.
Continue alternating arm raises, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.

1621.description: The Wide Stance Plank with Diagonal Leg Lift is a challenging core exercise that engages multiple muscle groups simultaneously, improving overall strength and stability.
instructions: Assume a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet wider than hip-width apart.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels.
Slowly lift one leg diagonally out to the side, keeping the leg straight and your hips square.
Hold the leg raise for a moment, then lower it back to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.

1622.description: The Wide Stance Plank With Leg Lift is a core-strengthening exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the abdominals, obliques, and hip flexors. It challenges stability and balance while improving overall core strength and endurance.
instructions: Assume a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles and keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly lift one leg off the ground, keeping the knee bent at a 90-degree angle and your leg parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for a few seconds, then lower your leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.

1127.description: The Windmill Switches is a full-body exercise that targets various muscle groups, improving overall strength, stability, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and arms extended out to your sides at shoulder height.
Shift your weight to your left leg and hinge at the hips to lower your torso, reaching your right hand down toward the outside of your left foot.
Pause, then engage your core to return to the starting position, simultaneously raising your right arm back up to shoulder height.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side, shifting your weight to the right leg and reaching your left hand toward the outside of your right foot.

1892.description: The X Abs exercise is a dynamic core strengthening exercise that targets multiple abdominal muscles, including the rectus abdominis, obliques, and transverse abdominis. It helps improve overall core stability and strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, engaging your core muscles.
Raise your arms out to the sides, parallel to the floor, with palms facing down.
Keeping your upper body stationary, twist your torso to the right, reaching your right arm back and your left arm forward.
Return to the starting position and repeat the twisting motion to the left side.
Alternate between right and left sides, maintaining control and stability throughout the movement.

1404.description: The Zercher Good Morning is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the posterior chain, core, and upper back. It helps build strength and stability throughout the body.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell in the crook of your elbows at chest height.
Keeping your core braced, send your hips back while maintaining a neutral spine. Lower the barbell toward the floor, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Pause briefly, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring proper form and control throughout the exercise.

1962.description: The Zercher Squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core. It is an effective exercise for building overall lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy surface, such as a bench or box, with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your toes slightly turned out.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your torso, tucking your elbows in front of your body and gripping the surface with your hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, descend into a full squat position, ensuring your knees track over your toes and your hips drop below parallel.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
